about.changesModal.noNotesWithLink: Shows on the About page's release notes dialog when the current build has no notes recorded. `<link>` wraps the words in the middle of the sentence and must stay around exactly that phrase; it renders as a link to GitHub's release page and needs no href text of its own.
about.devBuildWarning: Shows on the About page when Reaper is running a development build instead of a numbered release. `dev` is a literal word shown in a code style, not a placeholder; keep the word "dev" as it is written in the source, since it names the build channel.
about.reaperDataDetail: A fragment on the About page's storage line, listing what the app's main database holds. `{size}` is a formatted size (for example "1.2 GB"). The words after the comma are a plain list of nouns: decisions, audit trail, credentials.
about.reaperVersion: The version heading on the About page. `{version}` is Reaper's version string (for example "2026.8.1" or "dev").
about.rebuildableCacheDetail: A fragment on the About page's storage line, listing what Reaper's disposable cache holds and can rebuild from scratch. `{size}` is a formatted size. The words after the comma are a plain list of nouns: watch history, ratings, lists.
about.update.newRelease: A notice on the About page saying a newer release exists. `{version}` is the new version string (for example "2026.9.1").
backup.download.failed: Shown in Settings → Backup when downloading a backup file does not start. {error} is the raw error text from the browser or server, passed through as written.
backup.restore.cancelFailed: Shown in the Restore flow when canceling a staged restore fails. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
backup.restore.checkingFile: Progress line shown while Reaper reads an uploaded backup file before restoring it. {fileName} is the file name the operator picked or dropped, exactly as their operating system reports it.
backup.restore.chooseFailed: Shown when Reaper cannot read a file the operator picked to restore. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
backup.restore.dropzonePrompt: The restore screen's file drop area. <btn>choose one</btn> is a button that opens a file picker; keep it as a short clickable phrase.
backup.restore.fromSavedSuffix: A fragment appended after a backup's saved date, forming one sentence with another key such as "Reaper {version}, saved {when}". {when} is a formatted date and time.
backup.restore.fromVersion: Names which Reaper release a backup file was made with, shown beside its details before a restore. {version} is a version number like "2024.3".
backup.restore.restartFailed: Shown when Reaper does not come back up after a restore triggers a restart. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
backup.restore.restoreFailed: Shown when starting a restore fails outright. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
chip.sentence.below: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.below. The scoring outcome: the item scored under the operator's own remove threshold.
chip.sentence.below_threshold: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.below_threshold. The scoring outcome with the numbers shown. {score} and {threshold} are both plain integers on Reaper's 0-100 removal-pressure scale.
chip.sentence.came_back: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.came_back. The item left the library before and came back; Reaper holds it for a set period afterward. {days_left_span} (chip.text) is a humanized span like '3 weeks' derived from a raw day count.
chip.sentence.came_back_unknown: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.came_back_unknown. Same reason as chip.text.came_back, for a row where the countdown itself could not be recovered. No params.
chip.sentence.coverage: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.coverage. Too little of the item's evidence could be read for Reaper to score it with confidence, so it is kept rather than guessed at.
chip.sentence.kept.curated_list: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.curated_list. It is on an operator-curated protected list (Settings → Lists).
chip.sentence.kept.custom: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.custom. An operator-authored custom keep rule fired for this item.
chip.sentence.kept.dormancy: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.dormancy. It has not sat unwatched long enough yet to be considered for removal (the minimum-dormancy protection).
chip.sentence.kept.hand_spare: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.hand_spare. The operator manually spared this item.
chip.sentence.kept.no_history: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.no_history. Reaper has no watch history for it at all, so it is kept to be safe rather than guessed at.
chip.sentence.kept.others_watching: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.others_watching. {count} is the same pluralized count of other simultaneous viewers.
chip.sentence.kept.others_watching_unkno: The full-sentence fallback of chip.sentence.kept.others_watching for when the exact count of other viewers could not be recorded. No params.
chip.sentence.kept.popularity: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.popularity, with the same {count} and {window_days_window} params.
chip.sentence.kept.popularity_plain: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.popularity_plain. People here still watch it, without a specific count or window recorded for this row.
chip.sentence.kept.rating: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.rating, with the same {value_fixed1} and {source_label} params.
chip.sentence.kept.rating_plain: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.rating_plain. It is well rated, without a specific number or source recorded for this row.
chip.sentence.kept.returned: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.returned. It came back after leaving the library before. A rare, older reason: the current version of this hold normally shows as came_back/came_back_unknown instead.
chip.sentence.kept.season.airing: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.season.airing. Kept because the show is still running.
chip.sentence.kept.season.first: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.season.first. Kept because it is the earliest season on disk.
chip.sentence.kept.season.incomplete: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.season.incomplete. Kept because episodes are missing from it.
chip.sentence.kept.season.keep_all: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.season.keep_all. Kept because the operator's keep-last rule keeps every season on this show.
chip.sentence.kept.season.keep_last: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.season.keep_last, with the same {keep_last} count.
chip.sentence.kept.season.midbinge: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.season.midbinge. Kept because someone is partway through the show.
chip.sentence.kept.season.progress_histo: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.season.progress_history_short. Kept because the watch history is too short to tell who is mid-binge.
chip.sentence.kept.season.rule: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.season.rule. Kept because a generic season-keep rule kept it, with no more specific wording.
chip.sentence.kept.season.specials: The full-sentence version of chip.text.kept.season.specials. Kept because specials are never removed automatically.
chip.sentence.kept.streaming_now: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.streaming_now. Someone is actively watching it right now.
chip.sentence.kept.unknown: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.unknown. Some protection applies, but which one could not be identified for the chip.
chip.sentence.kept.unmanaged: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.unmanaged. The file is not tracked by Sonarr or Radarr, so Reaper has no safe way to remove it. A retired reason kept only for older stored rows.
chip.sentence.kept.whitelisted: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.kept.whitelisted. It is on a list the operator curates themselves (a generic keep list, distinct from a specific named list).
chip.sentence.look.comparable: The full-sentence version of chip.text.look.comparable. Reaper made an actual comparison: a season it would prune had more watchers than a season a keep rule protects, and left the call to the operator.
chip.sentence.look.unknowable: The full-sentence version of chip.text.look.unknowable. Reaper could not tell who watched the seasons involved in a keep-rule conflict, and left the call to the operator.
chip.sentence.look.unsettled: The full-sentence version of chip.text.look.unsettled. A check on this item could not be settled one way or the other, and was left for the operator to decide. A generic fallback used when neither comparable nor unknowable applies.
chip.sentence.match.ambiguous: The full-sentence version of chip.text.match.ambiguous. No params.
chip.sentence.match.conflicted: The full-sentence version of chip.text.match.conflicted, with the same {media_type} select between Radarr and Sonarr.
chip.sentence.match.unmatched: The full-sentence version of chip.text.match.unmatched. No params.
chip.sentence.match.unreadable: The full-sentence version of chip.text.match.unreadable. No params.
chip.sentence.unknown_checks: The full-sentence version of the same status shown compactly by chip.text.unknown_checks. One or more protections could not be checked for this item, though that did not decide its status on its own.
chip.text.below: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card. The scoring outcome: the item scored under the operator's own remove threshold. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.below; keep the same meaning in both.
chip.text.below_threshold: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card. The scoring outcome with the numbers shown. {score} and {threshold} are both plain integers on Reaper's 0-100 removal-pressure scale. chip.text.came_back: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card. chip.text.came_back_unknown: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card. Same reason as chip.text.came_back, for a row where the countdown itself could not be recovered. No params. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.came_back_unknown; keep the same meaning in both.
chip.text.coverage: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card. Too little of the item's evidence could be read for Reaper to score it with confidence, so it is kept rather than guessed at. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.coverage; keep the same meaning in both.
chip.text.kept.curated_list: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. It is on an operator-curated protected list (Settings → Lists). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.curated_list.
chip.text.kept.custom: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. An operator-authored custom keep rule fired for this item. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.custom.
chip.text.kept.dormancy: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. It has not sat unwatched long enough yet to be considered for removal (the minimum-dormancy protection). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.dormancy.
chip.text.kept.hand_spare: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. The operator manually spared this item. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.hand_spare.
chip.text.kept.no_history: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. Reaper has no watch history for it at all, so it is kept to be safe rather than guessed at. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.no_history.
chip.text.kept.others_watching: The compact status-chip fragment for 'someone else is watching it right now', prefixed 'Kept, '. {count} is a plain count of other simultaneous viewers, pluralized. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.others_watching.
chip.text.kept.others_watching_unknown: The compact status-chip fallback of chip.text.kept.others_watching for when the exact count of other viewers could not be recorded. No params.
chip.text.kept.popularity: The compact status-chip fragment for 'N people watched it recently', prefixed 'Kept, '. {count} is a plain pluralized count of distinct viewers; {window_days_window} is a humanized window like 'year' derived from a raw day count. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.popularity.
chip.text.kept.popularity_plain: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. People here still watch it, without a specific count or window recorded for this row. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.popularity_plain.
chip.text.kept.rating: The compact status-chip fragment for 'well rated', prefixed 'Kept, '. {value_fixed1} is a rating rounded to one decimal place; {source_label} is the rating source's display name, composed from why.source.*. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.rating.
chip.text.kept.rating_plain: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. It is well rated, without a specific number or source recorded for this row. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.rating_plain.
chip.text.kept.returned: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. It came back after leaving the library before. A rare, older reason: the current version of this hold normally shows as came_back/came_back_unknown instead. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.returned.
chip.text.kept.season.airing: The compact status-chip fragment for a TV season kept because the show is still running, prefixed 'Kept, '. The same reason the why-panel shows as why.season_keep.airing (or, for progress_history_short, as a keep-rule row with no season_keep counterpart). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.season.airing.
chip.text.kept.season.first: The compact status-chip fragment for a TV season kept because it is the earliest season on disk, prefixed 'Kept, '. The same reason the why-panel shows as why.season_keep.first (or, for progress_history_short, as a keep-rule row with no season_keep counterpart). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.season.first.
chip.text.kept.season.incomplete: The compact status-chip fragment for a TV season kept because episodes are missing from it, prefixed 'Kept, '. The same reason the why-panel shows as why.season_keep.incomplete (or, for progress_history_short, as a keep-rule row with no season_keep counterpart). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.season.incomplete.
chip.text.kept.season.keep_all: The compact status-chip fragment for a TV season kept because the operator's keep-last rule keeps every season on this show, prefixed 'Kept, '. The same reason the why-panel shows as why.season_keep.keep_all (or, for progress_history_short, as a keep-rule row with no season_keep counterpart). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.season.keep_all.
chip.text.kept.season.keep_last: The compact status-chip fragment for a season kept by the keep-last-N rule, prefixed 'Kept, '. {keep_last} is the operator's configured number of newest seasons to keep, a plain integer. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.season.keep_last.
chip.text.kept.season.midbinge: The compact status-chip fragment for a TV season kept because someone is partway through the show, prefixed 'Kept, '. The same reason the why-panel shows as why.season_keep.midbinge (or, for progress_history_short, as a keep-rule row with no season_keep counterpart). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.season.midbinge.
chip.text.kept.season.progress_history_s: The compact status-chip fragment for a TV season kept because the watch history is too short to tell who is mid-binge, prefixed 'Kept, '. The same reason the why-panel shows as why.season_keep.progress_history_short (or, for progress_history_short, as a keep-rule row with no season_keep counterpart). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.season.progress_history_short.
chip.text.kept.season.rule: The compact status-chip fragment for a TV season kept because a generic season-keep rule kept it, with no more specific wording, prefixed 'Kept, '. The same reason the why-panel shows as why.season_keep.rule (or, for progress_history_short, as a keep-rule row with no season_keep counterpart). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.season.rule.
chip.text.kept.season.specials: The compact status-chip fragment for a TV season kept because specials are never removed automatically, prefixed 'Kept, '. The same reason the why-panel shows as why.season_keep.specials (or, for progress_history_short, as a keep-rule row with no season_keep counterpart). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.season.specials.
chip.text.kept.streaming_now: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. Someone is actively watching it right now. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.streaming_now.
chip.text.kept.unknown: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. Some protection applies, but which one could not be identified for the chip. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.unknown.
chip.text.kept.unmanaged: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. The file is not tracked by Sonarr or Radarr, so Reaper has no safe way to remove it. A retired reason kept only for older stored rows. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.unmanaged.
chip.text.kept.whitelisted: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card, prefixed 'Kept, '. It is on a list the operator curates themselves (a generic keep list, distinct from a specific named list). Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.kept.whitelisted.
chip.text.look.comparable: The compact status-chip fragment for the 'Needs a look' tone, prefixed 'Needs a look, '. Reaper made an actual comparison: a season it would prune had more watchers than a season a keep rule protects, and left the call to the operator. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.look.comparable.
chip.text.look.unknowable: The compact status-chip fragment for the 'Needs a look' tone, prefixed 'Needs a look, '. Reaper could not tell who watched the seasons involved in a keep-rule conflict, and left the call to the operator. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.look.unknowable.
chip.text.look.unsettled: The compact status-chip fragment for the 'Needs a look' tone, prefixed 'Needs a look, '. A check on this item could not be settled one way or the other, and was left for the operator to decide. A generic fallback used when neither comparable nor unknowable applies. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.look.unsettled.
chip.text.match.ambiguous: The compact status-chip fragment for a title that looks like more than one thing in Plex, so Reaper cannot be sure which one it is looking at. No params. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.match.ambiguous.
chip.text.match.conflicted: The compact status-chip fragment for when Plex and Sonarr/Radarr describe the same title differently. {media_type} selects between 'Radarr' (movies) and 'Sonarr' (TV); only one branch renders. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.match.conflicted.
chip.text.match.unmatched: The compact status-chip fragment for a title Reaper could not find in Plex at all. No params. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.match.unmatched.
chip.text.match.unreadable: The compact status-chip fragment for a title whose Plex match data Reaper found but could not read. No params. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.match.unreadable.
chip.text.unknown_checks: The compact status-chip fragment on a review-queue card. One or more protections could not be checked for this item, though that did not decide its status on its own. Its full-sentence twin is chip.sentence.unknown_checks; keep the same meaning in both.
common.editNamed: The accessible label on an Edit button next to a named item (a connected service, a saved list). `{name}` is the operator's own name for that item, typed by them, not translated.
common.removeNamedQuestion: A confirmation question shown before removing a named item (a connected service, a saved list). `{name}` is the operator's own name for it, typed by them, not translated.
common.scanStartFailed: An inline error shown where a scan was just asked to start and the request failed. `{message}` is the error text the server sent back, already in plain language; render it as given.
error.auth.api_key_invalid: Answered to an API-key client whose key was rejected; not a browser-facing screen.
error.auth.api_key_read_denied: Answered to an API-key client whose key can't read this; not a browser-facing screen. `{exclusions}` is a plain-English list of what an API key CANNOT read, already joined by the server.
error.auth.api_key_throttled: Answered to an API-key client whose key was rejected; not a browser-facing screen.
error.auth.api_key_write_denied: Answered to an API-key client whose key can't write this; not a browser-facing screen. `{permissions}` is a plain-English list of what an API key CAN write, already joined by the server.
error.auth.arm_deletion_password_mismatc: Shown in Settings, Safety, when confirming Turn deletion on with the admin password.
error.auth.change_password_mismatch: Shown in Settings, Security, when changing the admin password. Nested by security.form.changeFailedError, which states that the password was not changed.
error.auth.csrf_blocked: Shown wherever a request is refused by Reaper's own cross-site protection; rare, and not tied to one screen.
error.auth.forget_watch_password_mismatc: Shown in Settings when confirming Forget this record with the admin password.
error.auth.forward_origin_has_path: Shown in Settings when saving the application's external address.
error.auth.forward_origin_invalid: Shown in Settings when saving the application's external address.

error.auth.not_authenticated: Shown wherever a request needs a signed-in session and none exists.
error.auth.password_hashing_busy: Shown on the sign-in screen under heavy concurrent load.

error.auth.sign_in_busy: Shown on the sign-in screen under heavy concurrent load.

error.instances.not_found: Shown in Settings, Services, while adding or editing a connection.

error.instances.wrong_kind_for_seerr_ser: Shown in Settings, Services, while adding or editing a connection.

error.runs.preflight_no_plex: Shown when planning, confirming, or stopping a reap, on the Reap page.
error.runs.preflight_no_tautulli: Shown when planning, confirming, or stopping a reap, on the Reap page.
error.safety.deletion_off: Shown when starting a reap while deletion is off, on the Reap page.
error.safety.recovery_mode_active: Shown when starting a reap while deletion is off, on the Reap page.
error.scan.already_running: Shown when a background scan is refused because one is already running. No params.
error.scan.gate_unimplemented: Shown when a scan cannot start, on the Jobs panel. `{gate}` is the protection's own id, exactly as the policy stores it.
error.scan.list_gate_missing_list: Shown when a scan cannot start, on the Jobs panel.
error.scan.missing_sources: Shown when a scan cannot start, on the Jobs panel.
error.scan.source_unreachable: Shown when a background scan stops because a configured source couldn't be reached. `{error}` is the underlying service's own error text, passed through as written.
error.scan.unexpected: Shown when a background scan stops on an error Reaper didn't otherwise account for. `{error}` is the underlying error's own text, passed through as written.
error.settings.accent_color_invalid: Shown in Settings, General, when saving the accent color.
error.settings.application_url_invalid: Shown in Settings, General, when saving the application URL.
error.settings.bad_cron: Shown in Settings, Schedule, when saving a custom schedule. `{reason}` is the underlying failure's own plain-English text, passed through as written.
error.settings.desktop_only: Shown in Settings, General; these controls exist only in the desktop app.
error.settings.discord_webhook_invalid: Shown in Settings, Notifications, when saving the Discord webhook.
error.settings.dock_icon_macos_only: Shown in Settings, General, on the macOS app only.
error.settings.external_url_invalid: Shown in Settings, General, when saving the external URL.
error.settings.folder_list_unreachable: Shown in Settings, Services, while mapping a connection's root folders. `{error}` is the underlying service's own error text, passed through as written.
error.settings.instance_base_url_invalid: Shown in Settings, Services, when saving a connection's address.
error.settings.launcher_conf_write_faile: Shown in Settings, General, on the desktop app only.
error.settings.no_api_key: Shown in Settings, Security, before an API key has been generated.
error.settings.no_password_set_for_armin: Shown in Settings, Safety, when turning deletion on.
error.settings.notification_language_unk: Shown in Settings, Notifications, when saving the Discord notification language. `{tag}` is the BCP 47 tag the browser sent, exactly as sent.
error.settings.recovery_mode_blocks_armi: Shown in Settings, Safety, when turning deletion on.
error.settings.service_list_unreachable: Shown in Settings, Services, while mapping a Seerr portal's services. `{error}` is the underlying service's own error text, passed through as written.
error.settings.timezone_unknown: Shown in Settings, General, when saving the timezone.
error.settings.trusted_proxy_invalid: Shown in Settings, Security, when saving trusted proxies. `{entry}` is the address or range the operator typed, exactly as they entered it.
error.settings.unknown_runnable_job: Shown in Settings, Schedule, or the Jobs panel's Run now. `{job_id}` is the job's own id, as Settings, Schedule names it.
error.settings.unknown_schedulable_job: Shown in Settings, Schedule. `{job_id}` is the job's own id, as Settings, Schedule names it.
error.settings.unknown_service_kind: Shown in Settings, Services, while adding a connection. `{value}` is the value the operator typed or the field itself computed, exactly as it was read.
error.simulate.no_scan: Shown in the Policy editor's simulator panel.
error.transport.bad_reply: Shown wherever a request to the server fails below the level Reaper's own catalog covers: no reply, a reply with no reason in it, or a reply the browser couldn't read. Not tied to one screen.
error.transport.request_failed: Shown wherever a request to the server fails below the level Reaper's own catalog covers: no reply, a reply with no reason in it, or a reply the browser couldn't read. Not tied to one screen.
error.transport.server_unreachable: Shown wherever a request to the server fails below the level Reaper's own catalog covers: no reply, a reply with no reason in it, or a reply the browser couldn't read. Not tied to one screen.
error.whitelist.unknown_item: Shown when a hand override refers to an item outside Reaper's recent scans. `{keep_scans}` is how many recent scans Reaper keeps a record for, pluralized.
format.souls: A shared plural count used on more than one screen (for example the reap plan and reap confirmation) to say how many titles are involved: "1 soul", "7 souls". "Soul" is Reaper's own playful word for a counted title, not a religious term; translate it as a light, informal word for "item" or "title" if a literal translation of "soul" would sound out of place. `{n}` is the count and drives the plural form.
format.spareExpiredOn: A fragment shown wherever a hand-kept item's temporary spare has run out, naming the date it expired. `{date}` is a formatted calendar date. This text is nested inside other status strings rather than shown alone.
format.spareLeft: A count of days left on a temporary spare (a hand-kept item Reaper will judge again once the countdown ends): "3 days left". `{n}` is the day count and drives the plural form; it also appears a second time inside the plural branches as the literal number to display.
format.spareShort: A very short "days left" abbreviation for a spare, used where space is tight (for example a small status chip): "3d". `{n}` is the day count. Keep this as short as the source; a longer translation may not fit its control.
format.spareStillKept: A fragment appended after the spare's expiry date, explaining that the item stays kept until the next scan reconsiders it. `{expiredOn}` is another composed string (the "expired on" date sentence) inserted before this one; write this fragment to read naturally right after a date.
format.spareUntil: A fragment saying a hand-kept item is spared until a given date: "Kept until {date}". `{date}` is a formatted calendar date.
format.totalWithUnknown: A fragment combining a known total with a count of items whose size Reaper could not measure, used wherever a total size is shown: "1.2 GB, 3 sizes unknown". `{known}` is an already-formatted size string; `{n}` is the count of unmeasured items and drives the plural form.
general.desktop.trayHelp: Help text under the tray/menu bar icon setting above, explaining what turning it off costs: the operator has to use a system tool (Activity Monitor or Task Manager) to quit Reaper instead. `{platform}` again selects between the macOS wording and the wording for other systems; Activity Monitor and Task Manager are the actual names of those operating systems' own tools and should stay recognizable.
general.desktop.trayLabel: The label for a setting in the desktop app's General settings, controlling the small persistent icon Reaper keeps while running. Only shown in the desktop build, never in the web app. `{platform}` selects the wording for macOS ("Menu bar icon") versus other systems ("Tray icon"); keep both branches of the `select` even if your language would normally use one word for both.
jobs.cron.custom: The Jobs screen's plain-language summary of a schedule, used when the schedule is too irregular to describe in words. {cron} is the raw schedule expression (a cron string, e.g. "0 3 * * 1"), shown as-is since it is not natural language.
jobs.cron.everyDayAt: The Jobs screen's plain-language summary of a schedule that runs once a day. {at} is a formatted time of day, like "3:00 AM".
jobs.cron.everyNDaysAt: The Jobs screen's plain-language summary of a schedule that runs every few days. {n} is a whole number of days, {at} a formatted time of day.
jobs.cron.everyNHours: The Jobs screen's plain-language summary of a schedule that repeats every few hours. {n} is a whole number of hours.
jobs.cron.monthlyAt: The Jobs screen's plain-language summary of a schedule that runs once a month. {n} is the day of the month as an ordinal (1st, 2nd, 3rd...), and {at} a formatted time of day. Keep the ordinal suffix rule for your language; the English form is built into this ICU plural, but a translation may need its own ordinal rules.
jobs.cron.weeklyAt: The Jobs screen's plain-language summary of a schedule that runs once a week. {day} is a weekday name (e.g. "Monday"), {at} a formatted time of day.
jobs.leavingSoon.counts: On the Jobs screen, the count of titles currently on Plex's "Leaving Soon" shelf (a Plex feature Reaper can populate with titles about to be removed). <movieNum> and <seasonNum> wrap the two numbers for styling; keep the tags around the numbers they wrap. {movieCount}/{seasonCount} are counts, and {movies}/{seasons} are the same counts again, used only to pick the singular or plural word "movie(s)"/"season(s)".
jobs.leavingSoon.countsAtLastUpdate: The same shelf count as jobs.leavingSoon.counts, but phrased in the past tense for a status line that reports the last update rather than the current state. Same params.
jobs.leavingSoon.offNotice: Shown on the Jobs screen when the "Leaving Soon" update job is off. <btn>Turn it on in Plex → Leaving Soon</btn> is a link; "Plex" and "Leaving Soon" are Plex's own feature names and should stay recognizable, ideally matching how Plex itself is localized.
jobs.leavingSoon.renaming: Shown on the Jobs screen after the owner renames the shelf but before Reaper has moved it. {was} is the name Plex still shows, the owner's own text. "This update" means the job described by this row.
jobs.leavingSoon.title: A job row's heading on the Jobs screen. {shelf} is the fixed phrase "Leaving Soon shelf" (jobs.leavingSoon.shelfName), nested in as a fragment.
jobs.leavingSoon.updateFailed: Shown on the Jobs screen when refreshing the Leaving Soon shelf fails. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
jobs.leavingSoon.updateNowAria: Screen-reader label for the "Run now" button on the Leaving Soon job row. {shelf} is the fixed phrase "Leaving Soon shelf", nested in as a fragment.
jobs.leavingSoon.updatingAria: Screen-reader label shown while the Leaving Soon job is running. {shelf} is the fixed phrase "Leaving Soon shelf", nested in as a fragment. The ellipsis (…) is intentional, matching a busy/in-progress state.
jobs.maintenance.scheduleText: The Jobs screen's one-line schedule summary for the housekeeping (maintenance) job. {cron} is a plain-language schedule description composed from the jobs.cron.* keys above, and {when} is a formatted relative time like "in 2 hours".
jobs.result.history_no_source: Shown on the Jobs page's Full watch-history update row after it runs with no Tautulli connected. No params.
jobs.result.history_partial: Shown on the Jobs page's Full watch-history update row after a sweep that couldn't read every play. `{unservable}` is the count of plays Tautulli refused to return.
jobs.result.history_update_failed: Shown on the Jobs page's Full watch-history update row after the sweep fails outright. No params.
jobs.result.history_updated: Shown on the Jobs page's Full watch-history update row after a clean sweep. No params.
jobs.result.lists_partial: Shown on the Jobs page's Refresh your lists row after some but not all lists refreshed. `{checked}` is how many refreshed; `{failed}` is how many couldn't be checked.
jobs.result.lists_plex_not_connected: Shown on the Jobs page's Refresh your lists row when Plex-sourced lists exist but no Plex server is linked. No params.
jobs.result.lists_plex_unreachable: Shown on the Jobs page's Refresh your lists row when Plex-sourced lists exist but Plex couldn't be reached. No params.
jobs.result.lists_refresh_failed: Shown on the Jobs page's Refresh your lists row when the refresh fails outright or nothing could be checked. No params.
jobs.result.lists_refreshed: Shown on the Jobs page's Refresh your lists row after every list refreshed cleanly. No params.
jobs.result.ratings_refresh_failed: Shown on the Jobs page's Refresh IMDb ratings row when the download or load fails. No params.
jobs.result.ratings_refreshed: Shown on the Jobs page's Refresh IMDb ratings row after a clean refresh. No params.
jobs.result.ratings_refreshed_partial: Shown on the Jobs page's Refresh IMDb ratings row when the download landed but an unusual share of it couldn't be read. No params.
jobs.result.ratings_up_to_date: Shown on the Jobs page's Refresh IMDb ratings row when the dataset was already refreshed recently enough to skip. No params.
jobs.result.scan_failed: Shown on the Jobs page's automatic-scan row when a scheduled scan crashes outright and writes no snapshot. No params.
jobs.result.shelf_failed: Shown on the Jobs page's Leaving Soon row, and on the Plex panel's shelf status line, when one or more libraries' shelves failed to update. `{libraries}` is a comma-joined list of the library names that failed.
jobs.result.shelf_no_libraries: Shown on the Jobs page's Leaving Soon row, and on the Plex panel's shelf status line, when the shelf is on but no library has it enabled. No params.
jobs.result.shelf_preview: Shown on the Jobs page's Leaving Soon row, and on the Plex panel's shelf status line, when the pass ran but Reaper isn't allowed to write to Plex right now, so nothing was written. No params.
jobs.result.shelf_updated: Shown on the Jobs page's Leaving Soon row, and on the Plex panel's shelf status line, after a clean shelf update. `{added}` and `{removed}` are counts, formatted with the browser's own thousands separator.
jobs.result.update_available: Shown on the Jobs page's Check for updates row, matching the About page's own wording, when a newer released version exists. `{latest}` is that version number.
jobs.result.update_check_failed: Shown on the Jobs page's Check for updates row when the check couldn't reach GitHub or couldn't make sense of the answer. No params.
jobs.result.update_checks_off: Shown on the Jobs page's Check for updates row when update checks are turned off. No params.
jobs.result.update_dev_behind: Shown on the Jobs page's Check for updates row, matching the About page's own wording, when running a dev build that is now behind the dev branch. No params.
jobs.result.update_dev_current: Shown on the Jobs page's Check for updates row, matching the About page's own wording, when running a dev build that matches the dev branch. No params.
jobs.result.update_up_to_date: Shown on the Jobs page's Check for updates row, matching the About page's own wording, when running the newest release. No params.
jobs.row.editAria: Screen-reader label for a job row's edit button. {title} is that job's own name, e.g. "Scan" or "Watch history sync".
jobs.row.runNowAria: Screen-reader label for a job row's "Run now" button. {title} is that job's own name.
jobs.row.runningAria: Screen-reader label shown while a job is running. {title} is that job's own name. The ellipsis (…) is intentional, matching a busy/in-progress state.
jobs.row.startFailed: Shown on the Jobs screen when starting a job by hand fails. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
jobs.scan.scheduleText: The Jobs screen's one-line schedule summary for the library scan job. Same params and composition as jobs.maintenance.scheduleText.
jobs.schedule.defaultHelp: Help text under a job's schedule field, naming the built-in default schedule. {cron} is a plain-language schedule description composed from the jobs.cron.* keys above. "Run now" is a button label elsewhere on the same screen; keep the wording consistent with it.
jobs.schedule.zoneHelp: Help text explaining which time zone a job's schedule uses. {zone} is a time zone name or offset, e.g. "America/New_York" or "UTC-5". "Settings" and "General" name another screen in the app; keep them matching that screen's own labels.
jobs.status.flashSentence: A short-lived status line shown right after a job runs. {lead} is a fixed lead-in word like "Done" or "Failed" (composed elsewhere), and {text} is the job's own result summary. This joins the two with a colon; a language that does not use a colon this way may need a different joiner.
jobs.status.lastRunFailed: Job status line reporting the last run failed. {since} is a relative time like "2 hours ago"; the <exact> tag wraps an exact date and time shown as extra detail (e.g. in a tooltip), containing {date} and {time}.
jobs.status.lastRunFailedReason: Same as jobs.status.lastRunFailed, with a {reason} for the failure added inside the <exact> detail. {reason} is a short, already-plain-language explanation.
jobs.status.lastRunOk: Job status line reporting the last run succeeded. Same {since}/<exact>/{date}/{time} shape as jobs.status.lastRunFailed.
jobs.when.inHours: A relative time used in job schedule summaries, for a run happening in the next few hours. {hours} is a whole number; "hr" is a fixed abbreviation and should be translated to your language's own short form for "hours," or left as a short abbreviation if none exists.
jobs.when.inMinutes: A relative time used in job schedule summaries, for a run happening in the next few minutes. {mins} is a whole number; "min" is a fixed abbreviation for "minutes."
lists.ago.days: A relative time fragment nested inside another key's {when} slot on the Settings → Lists screen (`lists.meta.lastChecked`), meaning "N days ago". An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
lists.ago.hours: A relative time fragment nested inside another key's {when} slot on the Settings → Lists screen (`lists.meta.lastChecked`), meaning "N hours ago". An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
lists.ago.minutes: A relative time fragment nested inside another key's {when} slot on the Settings → Lists screen (`lists.meta.lastChecked`), meaning "N minutes ago". An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
lists.checkFailed: Shown on the Settings → Lists screen when a list's manual "Check now" fails. {error} is the plain-language error text from the app Reaper talked to (Plex, Sonarr, or Radarr), passed through as it was written, not translated further.
lists.describe.cached: A short status fragment on a list row: how many titles from an unreachable source are still being kept from the last successful check. {titles} nests `lists.titleCount` (an already-pluralized "N titles").
lists.describe.onIt: A short status fragment on a list row: how many titles the list currently protects. {titles} nests `lists.titleCount` (an already-pluralized "N titles").
lists.help.presetDescription: Help text under a built-in preset list (for example an IMDb Top 250 list) on the Add List screen. {label} is the preset's own display name, nested from `lists.presetLabel`.
lists.help.sourceLocked: Help text on the edit-list screen, explaining that a list's source (Plex collection, Sonarr/Radarr tag, and so on) can't be changed after creation. {sourceName} is the source kind's display name, for example "Plex collection".
lists.kindBadge.srOnly: Screen-reader-only text on a list's source badge, stating which apps a partly-exposed list actually protects in. Sonarr and Radarr are product names and stay untranslated. {exposedWords} nests `lists.mediaWords` ("movies", "shows", or "movies and shows"). An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
lists.loadError: Shown on the Settings → Lists screen when the list of curated lists itself fails to load. <btn> wraps a retry button; keep the tag, translate only the text inside it.
lists.loadErrorRetrying: The same load-failure notice as `lists.loadError`, shown while a retry is in flight. <btn> wraps the button's own "Trying…" label; keep the tag.
lists.mediaWords: A fragment naming which media types a list covers ("movies", "shows", or "movies and shows"), nested inside several other `lists.*` and badge strings. An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
lists.meta.across: A fragment on a list row stating how many Plex/Sonarr/Radarr servers the list spans. {n} is a plain server count. Ends with a trailing space because the caller appends more text after it; keep a trailing space in the translation too.
lists.meta.lastChecked: A fragment on a list row stating when it was last checked. {when} nests one of `lists.ago.days`/`lists.ago.hours`/`lists.ago.minutes`. Ends with a trailing space because the caller appends more text after it; keep a trailing space in the translation too.
lists.modal.addTypedTitle: The heading of the Add List modal once a source type has been chosen. {sourceName} is the source kind's display name, for example "IMDb list".
lists.partial.detail: A note on a list row explaining that only part of what the list covers is actually protected. {kept} nests `lists.partial.kept` (which media types are protected), {still} nests `lists.mediaWords` (which media types can still be removed), capitalized.
lists.partial.kept: A fragment stating which media types a partially-active list still protects. {words} nests `lists.mediaWords`. Ends with a trailing space because the caller appends more text after it; keep a trailing space in the translation too.
lists.plexError: Shown on the Settings → Lists screen when a 'Check now' could not reach Plex at all, so none of the Plex-backed lists were checked. {error} is Plex's own plain-language error text, passed through as written: never translate its contents, only the surrounding sentence.
lists.presetLabel: The display name of a built-in preset list, shown in the Add List screen's preset picker and reused as the list's default name. {key} in the fallback option is the raw preset id, shown only if a preset is added with no matching label; the named options ("IMDb Top 250", "IMDb Popular Movies") are the preset's actual name and should read as a proper title. An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
lists.protectingTitle: A tooltip title on a list's coverage badge, stating what it protects. {words} nests `lists.mediaWords`. An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
lists.removeButton: The Remove-list button's own label, which also serves as its busy state while the removal is in flight. An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
lists.removeError: Shown on the Settings → Lists screen when removing a list fails. {error} is the plain-language error text from the server, passed through as written.
lists.row.checkAriaLabel: Screen-reader label for a list row's "Check now" button, naming the list by {title} so several rows' buttons read distinctly. An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
lists.row.checkButton: The visible label of a list row's "Check now" button, and its busy state while a check is running. An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
lists.row.editAriaLabel: Screen-reader label for a list row's edit button, naming the list by {title} so several rows' buttons read distinctly.
lists.saveError: Shown on the Add/Edit List screen when saving a list fails. {error} is the plain-language error text from the server, passed through as written.
lists.sourceHint.imdbList: A one-line hint under a list row naming the IMDb list it follows. {id} is the IMDb list's own id string (for example "ls012345678"), shown as-is.
lists.sourceHint.plexCollectionNamed: A one-line hint under a list row naming the Plex collection and library it follows. {collection} is the collection's own name as set in Plex; {library} is the Plex library (section) name.
lists.sourceName: The display name of a list's source kind (a Plex collection, a Plex watchlist, a Sonarr/Radarr tag, or an IMDb list), shown in several places including `lists.help.sourceLocked` and `lists.modal.addTypedTitle`. Sonarr, Radarr, Plex and IMDb are product names and stay untranslated. An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
lists.submitButton: The Add/Save List button's own label, and its busy state while the request is in flight. An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
lists.titleCount: A pluralized title count ("1 title" / "N titles"), nested inside several other `lists.*` strings. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
login.localSheet.noLocalYetNotice: Help text on the sign-in screen, shown before a local (non-Plex) account exists. It explains that signing in with Plex first lets Reaper create the local account, and gives a fallback command-line path for Docker and snap installs. `reaper-admin create-admin --username admin` is a literal shell command; do not translate any part of it, including the flag name and the word "admin".
login.recovery.note: Help text on the sign-in screen's password-recovery step, explaining where to find the one-time recovery code. `recovery.txt` is a literal file name and must not be translated.
logs.description: Explains the in-app log viewer, at the top of the Logs screen. {limit} is a whole number of lines Reaper keeps in memory for this view.
logs.downloadError: Shown on the Logs screen when downloading the full log file fails. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
logs.downloadRetentionKnown: Note on the Logs screen about how many log files are kept on disk versus what the on-screen viewer shows. {n} is a whole number of files.
logs.lineCount: A count of log lines shown on the Logs screen, e.g. as a badge. {n} is a whole number.
logs.lineCountOfTotal: A count shown when the Logs screen is displaying only some of the available lines. {visible} and {total} are both whole numbers, already formatted with the browser's own number formatting (thousands separators etc.).
plex.connection.manualOption: An option label in the Plex connection picker for a manually-entered server address. {uri} is the server address the operator typed, shown as-is.
plex.connectionLabel.plain: A short label describing one discovered Plex server connection (its kind of link and its host). {kind} is a short connection-type word (for example "Local" or "Relay"); {host} is the server's address, shown as-is.
plex.connectionLabel.secure: The secure-connection twin of `plex.connectionLabel.plain`, for a link that is also encrypted. {kind} and {host} are the same as there; the trailing "secure" is a plain adjective, not a technical term to preserve literally.
plex.leavingSoon.enableHelp: Help text under the switch that turns the Plex shelf on. {shelf} is the name the server owner gave the shelf. It defaults to the English "Leaving Soon" but they can rename it to anything, so translate the sentence around it and leave the name itself alone.
plex.leavingSoon.enableLabel: Label for the switch that turns the Plex shelf on, on the Plex settings screen. {shelf} is the name the server owner gave the shelf. It defaults to the English "Leaving Soon" but they can rename it to anything, so translate the sentence around it and leave the name itself alone.
plex.leavingSoon.status.line: The status line under the Leaving Soon shelf on the Plex settings screen, stating when it last refreshed and what it currently holds. {since} is a relative time phrase; {movies} nests `plex.leavingSoon.status.moviesCount`; {seasons} nests `plex.leavingSoon.status.seasonsCount`; {held} is a short verb phrase ("held" or similar) agreeing with the counts before it.
plex.leavingSoon.status.moviesCount: A pluralized movie count ("1 movie" / "N movies"), nested inside `plex.leavingSoon.status.line`. {count} is the number shown; {n} drives the plural form and is the same number.
plex.leavingSoon.status.passLine: The status line under the Leaving Soon shelf on the Plex settings screen, after a pass that completed. `{result}` is the pass's own outcome, one of the `jobs.result.shelf_*` sentences, and `{line}` is `plex.leavingSoon.status.line` composed on its own. The period between them lives here so the outcome sentence is never edited after it is composed.
plex.leavingSoon.status.renaming: Shown on the Plex settings screen after the owner renames the shelf but before Reaper has moved it. {was} is the name Plex still shows, the owner's own text. "Update" here means Reaper's shelf update, the job that carries the new name across.
plex.leavingSoon.status.seasonsCount: A pluralized TV season count ("1 season" / "N seasons"), nested inside `plex.leavingSoon.status.line`. {count} is the number shown; {n} drives the plural form and is the same number.
plex.libraries.foundCount: A pluralized count of Plex libraries found during setup ("1 library found" / "N libraries found"). An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
plex.libraries.toggleLabel: The label on a per-library on/off switch during Plex library selection. {title} is the Plex library's own name, shown as-is.
plex.linked.said: A status line confirming which Plex server is currently linked. {server} is the server's own name as reported by Plex, shown as-is.
plex.linkedAccount.help: Help text under the Plex sign-in status, showing the linked account. {uri} is the account or server address, shown as-is.
plex.server.missingNamed: An error notice on the Plex settings screen: the server Reaper is configured to use no longer appears in the operator's Plex account. {name} is that server's own name as Reaper has it stored, shown as-is.
plex.serverSwitched.named: A confirmation shown after the operator switches which Plex server Reaper uses. {name} is the newly chosen server's own name, shown as-is.
plex.trashNotice.knownReadable: A warning on the Plex settings screen before emptying Plex's trash, when Reaper could read exactly how many items are in it. <strong> wraps the lead warning sentence; keep the tag. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {n} argument).
plex.trashNotice.knownUnreadable: The same warning as `plex.trashNotice.knownReadable`, for when Reaper could only read a lower bound on the trash count because some libraries could not be read. <strong> wraps the lead warning sentence; keep the tag. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {n} argument).
plex.trashNotice.unknown: The same warning as `plex.trashNotice.knownReadable`, for when Reaper could not read Plex's trash at all. <strong> wraps the lead warning sentence; keep the tag.
plex.waiting.approveWithLink: Shown while Reaper waits for the operator to finish signing in to Plex in a separate browser window or tab. <btn> wraps a link to reopen that window if it didn't appear; keep the tag, translate only the text inside it.
plex.watchEvidence.forgotten: A status line on the Plex settings screen: Reaper had to discard its recorded plays for some titles because they could no longer be matched, and will rebuild that record from what Plex shows on the next scan. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {n} argument).
plex.watchEvidence.holding: A status line on the Plex settings screen stating how many titles Reaper currently holds a watch-history record for. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {n} argument).
plex.watchEvidence.holdingClean: The same status as `plex.watchEvidence.holding`, with an added note that the last scan found every recorded play still readable. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {n} argument).
plex.watchEvidence.holdingUnreadable: The same status as `plex.watchEvidence.holding`, with an added note that some titles' recorded plays could not be read on the last scan. Two independent counts, each its own plural: {n} is the titles held, {items} is the titles with unreadable plays.
policyEditor.gateRow.thresholdAriaLabel: A screen-reader-only label on the number box beside a protection's on/off switch in the Policy Editor. `{label}` is that protection's own name, already translated (for example "Rating floor"), so the label reads as "Rating floor threshold".
policyEditor.hash.line: A debug line in the Policy Editor showing the stored policy's fingerprint. `{kind}` is "Movies" or "TV", and `{hash}` is a short hexadecimal code shown inside a `<hashCode>` tag (a monospace span). The hash itself is not translated.
policyEditor.header.badge: A small label in the Policy Editor header naming which app enforces this policy: Radarr for movies, Sonarr for TV. Both are product names and stay untranslated.
policyEditor.header.blurb: The one-line subtitle under the Policy Editor's title. `{mediaType}` selects between the TV wording and the movies wording; only one branch renders at a time.
policyEditor.header.title: The Policy Editor's page title, "TV policy" or "Movies policy" depending on which policy is open.
policyEditor.intent.newestSeasons: A fragment inside the policy summary sentence at the top of the TV Policy Editor (see `policyEditor.intent.paceTailWithClause`, which the whole sentence is built from). `{n}` is how many of the newest seasons of each show are kept.
policyEditor.intent.paceTailWithClause: The closing fragment of the one-sentence policy summary at the top of the editor: an already-translated clause plus a period. `{clause}` is one of the other `policyEditor.intent.*` fragments, or a per-run limit fragment. If no clause applies, only "." is shown instead.
policyEditor.intent.removesAtMost: A fragment in the policy summary sentence, used only when per-run limits are on. `{items}` is a formatted item count and `{size}` is a formatted data size (for example "1.2 TiB"); both come from the app's own number formatting, not raw numbers.
policyEditor.intent.unwatchedLessThan: A fragment in the policy summary sentence, shown only when the "keep anything watched recently" protection is on. `{span}` is a humanized duration, like "3 weeks", already formatted by the app.
policyEditor.intent.watchedByPeople: A fragment in the policy summary sentence, shown only when the popularity protection is on. `{n}` is the minimum number of distinct viewers that protection requires.
policyEditor.pace.per30DaysHeader: A small header in the Policy Editor's pace-limits card. "rolling" is wrapped in an `<em>` tag for emphasis, meaning the 30-day window always covers the most recent 30 days, not a fixed calendar period.
policyEditor.pointsBudget.leftToGiveOut: Shown in the Policy Editor's points-budget readout while the operator's rules add up to less than the fixed 100-point total. `{n}` is how many points remain unassigned.
policyEditor.pointsBudget.over: Shown in the same points-budget readout when the operator's rules add up to more than 100. `{n}` is by how many points the total is over.
policyEditor.pointsBudget.overNotice: A blocking notice in the Policy Editor when the operator's removal rules add up to more than the fixed 100-point total and the policy cannot be saved yet. `{total}` is the current sum, `{n}` is how many points must be removed.
policyEditor.pointsBudget.split: A small breakdown line in the points-budget readout. `{builtIn}` and `{yours}` are each a plain number, for the points assigned to Reaper's built-in signals versus the operator's own custom rules.
policyEditor.pointsBudget.totalUsed: The main points-budget readout in the Policy Editor. `{total}` is a plain number wrapped in a `<totalNum>` tag (rendered bold); "100" is the fixed denominator every policy's removal weights add up to and is never itself a placeholder.
policyEditor.pointsBudget.underNotice: A notice in the Policy Editor when the operator's rules add up to less than 100 points and the policy cannot be saved yet. `{total}` is the current sum, `{n}` is how many points remain to be given out.
policyEditor.protections.blurb: The blurb above the list of protections (hard keep rules) in the Policy Editor. "keep" is wrapped in an `<em>` tag for emphasis: a protection can only save a title, never mark one for removal.
policyEditor.ratingBar.fromVotes: A fragment appended after a rating bar's score, used only when that source needs a minimum vote count. `{votes}` is the minimum vote count; the message already includes its own leading space and a "+" is added around the number elsewhere, so this note only concerns the wording, not the punctuation.
policyEditor.ratingBar.pct: A rating-bar summary for a percentage-based rating source (Rotten Tomatoes). `{label}` is the source's own name (for example "Rotten Tomatoes audience"), already translated by `why.source.*`, and `{floor}` is the percentage threshold.
policyEditor.ratingBar.percentAriaLabel: A screen-reader-only label on a rating bar's percentage input. `{label}` is the rating source's own translated name.
policyEditor.ratingBar.removeAriaLabel: A screen-reader-only label on the button that removes one rating bar from the "keep well-rated titles" protection. `{label}` is that bar's source name.
policyEditor.ratingBar.scoreAriaLabel: A screen-reader-only label on a rating bar's 0-10 score input. `{label}` is the rating source's own translated name; the scale itself ("out of 10") is fixed and not a placeholder.
policyEditor.ratingBar.ten: A rating-bar summary for a 0-10 rating source (IMDb, TMDb, Trakt). `{score}` is the numeric floor, `{label}` is the source's translated name, and `{votes}` is either empty or the `policyEditor.ratingBar.fromVotes` fragment appended after it.
policyEditor.ratingBar.voteFloorAriaLabe: A screen-reader-only label on a rating bar's minimum-vote-count input. `{label}` is the rating source's own translated name.
policyEditor.ratingFloor.clearsBars: Explains how multiple rating bars combine in the "keep well-rated titles" protection. `{match}` selects between "clears any one of these bars" and "clears all of these bars", depending on whether the operator requires one match or every match.
policyEditor.ratingFloor.summary: The one-line summary of the "keep well-rated titles" protection. `{bars}` is a list of already-composed rating-bar phrases (from `policyEditor.ratingBar.ten` / `.pct`), joined together outside this string.
policyEditor.rewatch.echoEmpty: A live preview in the rewatch-probability protection card, shown when no title in the operator's own library yet clears the chosen percentage. `{pct}` is that percentage and `{total}` is how many titles were measured.
policyEditor.rewatch.echoNoRange: A live preview in the rewatch-probability card. `{pct}` is the chosen percentage, `{protectedCount}` of `{total}` is how many of the operator's own titles or shows this would protect, and `{mediaType}` selects between "shows" and "titles".
policyEditor.rewatch.echoWithRange: Same live preview as `policyEditor.rewatch.echoNoRange`, but with `{range}` inserted: an already-composed phrase (from `policyEditor.rewatch.rangeOver` / `.rangeTo` / `.rangeUnder`) describing the span of unwatched time this percentage covers.
policyEditor.rewatch.notEnoughScanned: Shown in the rewatch-probability card when too few titles have been scanned yet to compute the operator's own numbers. `{mediaType}` selects between "shows" and "titles".
policyEditor.rewatch.rangeOver: A fragment describing an open-ended span of unwatched time, nested inside `policyEditor.rewatch.echoWithRange`'s `{range}`. `{phrase}` is an already-composed duration phrase from `policyEditor.rewatch.yearsPhrase` or similar.
policyEditor.rewatch.rangeTo: A fragment describing a bounded span of unwatched time, nested the same way as `policyEditor.rewatch.rangeOver`. `{lo}` is the lower bound as a humanized duration, `{phrase}` the upper bound.
policyEditor.rewatch.rangeUnder: A fragment describing a span capped at an upper bound, nested the same way as `policyEditor.rewatch.rangeOver`. `{phrase}` is an already-composed duration phrase.
policyEditor.rewatch.underAbout: A fragment used when the span is described as roughly under a duration. `{phrase}` is an already-composed duration phrase.
policyEditor.rewatch.yearsPhrase: A duration phrase combining a unit label and a year count, nested inside the rewatch range fragments above. `{label}` is a translated unit word and `{n}` is the number of years, with its own singular/plural form.
policyEditor.rewatchCopy.bar: The label on the rewatch-probability protection's percentage bar itself. `{mediaType}` selects TV wording ("watched again") from movie wording ("watched"), since a show's later seasons can be its first watch of that show.
policyEditor.rewatchCopy.barLabel: Same wording as `policyEditor.rewatchCopy.bar`, used as the input's accessible label rather than its visible text; keep the two consistent.
policyEditor.rewatchCopy.help: The help paragraph under the "keep likely rewatches" protection when it only lowers the score rather than keeping outright. `{mediaType}` selects TV wording from movie wording.
policyEditor.rewatchCopy.holdHelp: The help paragraph for the stronger form of the same protection, which keeps a title outright once its rewatch chance clears a percentage. `{mediaType}` selects TV wording from movie wording.
policyEditor.rewatchCopy.holdName: The protection's own name when it keeps outright. `{mediaType}` selects "shows" from "titles".
policyEditor.rewatchCopy.name: The protection's own name when it only lowers the score. `{mediaType}` selects "shows" from "titles".
policyEditor.savebar.kindPolicy: Shown in the sticky save bar at the bottom of the Policy Editor when there are unsaved changes. `{kind}` is "Movies" or "TV", naming which policy is dirty.
policyEditor.savebar.policyBlockedNotice: A notice in the save bar when the policy cannot be saved yet. `{kind}` is "Movies" or "TV" and `{because}` is an already-composed reason (for example, the points budget being over 100).
policyEditor.savebar.savesOnlyKind: A notice in the save bar clarifying that Save only writes the currently open policy. `{kind}` and `{otherKind}` are each "Movies" or "TV" (whichever is open, and the other one), and `{appliesOnNextScan}` is an already-composed trailing clause about when the change takes effect.
policyEditor.seasonAdvisory.message: A live advisory next to the "keep last N seasons" input, wrapped in a `<coveredNum>` tag around the count. `{bounded}` selects whether the count is exact ("yes") or a floor ("up to"), `{covered}` is how many shows the setting protects nothing on, and `{total}` is how many shows were scanned.
policyEditor.signalProbe.historyCap: A note under a signal's live preview, shown only when the operator's watch history doesn't reach back as far as the signal's own window. `{span}` is a humanized duration: how far back the history actually goes.
policyEditor.signalProbe.said: The live "what this value would do" preview beside a signal's ramp control. `{lead}` is an already-composed lead-in phrase, and `{value}`, `{points}`, `{weight}` are each a plain number, individually wrapped in bold tags (`<valueNum>`, `<pointsNum>`, `<weightNum>`) by the render site.
policyEditor.signalRamp.addsAll: A label on the ramp control's upper end, where a signal is contributing every point it can. `{label}` is that signal's own translated name, already quoted in the source string.
policyEditor.signalRamp.setDefaultAriaLa: A screen-reader-only label on the button that resets one signal's ramp to its default. `{label}` is that signal's own translated name.
policyEditor.signalRamp.startsAdding: A label on the ramp control's lower end, where a signal begins contributing points. `{label}` is that signal's own translated name, already quoted in the source string.
policyEditor.signalRamp.stopsAdding: A label on a ramp control where a signal stops adding further points past this point. `{label}` is that signal's own translated name, already quoted in the source string.
policyEditor.signalRow.upToPoints: A signal row's point badge: "up to N points", with "up to" and "points" each in their own muted tag (`<mutedLead>`, `<mutedTail>`) around the bold number (`<weightNum>`). `{weight}` is that signal's maximum weight.
policyEditor.signalRow.weightAriaLabel: A screen-reader-only label on a signal's weight control. `{label}` is that signal's own translated name.
policyEditor.starting.stagedNotice: A banner shown after applying a starting-point preset to the Policy Editor, before the operator has saved. "Staged, not saved." is wrapped in a `<strong>` tag; "Save changes" names the button in the save bar and should match its own translation.
policyEditor.switchConfirm.message: A confirmation dialog shown when the operator tries to switch between the Movies and TV policy tabs while one has unsaved changes. `{kind}` is the policy with unsaved changes ("Movies" or "TV"), `{pending}` is the tab they are switching to.
policyEditor.units.person: A reusable singular/plural unit word, "person"/"people", nested into other messages that count viewers. `{n}` decides the plural form but is not itself shown by this entry.
policyEditor.units.season: A reusable singular/plural unit word, "season"/"seasons", nested into other messages that count seasons. `{n}` decides the plural form but is not itself shown by this entry.
policyRules.condemn.graded: A removal rule's one-line summary in the rule list, for a rule that adds points on a sliding scale. `{label}` is the field's translated name (`why.field.*`), `{phrase}` is an already-composed clause, and `{from}`/`{to}` are the point range this rule adds.
policyRules.condemn.simple: A removal rule's one-line summary for a flat-weight rule. `{label}` is the field's translated name, `{op}` is a translated comparison word (is / contains / at least, and so on), and `{value}` is the operator-typed comparison value.
policyRules.condition.generic: A keep rule's one-line summary for an ordinary field comparison. `{label}` is the field's translated name, `{op}` a translated comparison word, `{value}` the operator-typed value.
policyRules.condition.onList: A keep rule's summary when the rule matches a specific list by exact name. `{list}` is the list's own name as the operator typed it, quoted by the render site; it is never translated.
policyRules.condition.onListOp: A keep rule's summary when the rule matches lists by a name pattern rather than one exact name. `{op}` is a translated comparison word (contains, is, and so on) and `{list}` is the operator-typed pattern.
policyRules.fieldHelp.days_unwatched: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'days_unwatched' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.genre: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'genre' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.imdb_rating: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'imdb_rating' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.imdb_votes: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'imdb_votes' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.on_list: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'on_list' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.quality: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'quality' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.recent_watchers: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'recent_watchers' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.release_age: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'release_age' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.requested: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'requested' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.season_rank: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'season_rank' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.show_ended: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'show_ended' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.size_bytes: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'size_bytes' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.streaming_now: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'streaming_now' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.watchers_all_time: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'watchers_all_time' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldHelp.whitelisted: A help paragraph in the Policy Editor's field picker, shown when the operator selects the 'whitelisted' field for a custom rule. It is standalone prose with no params, explaining a subtlety of how the field is measured. Translate it as a full paragraph.
policyRules.fieldUnit.days_unwatched: A short fixed unit word shown in the same box as the number, for a rule on the 'days_unwatched' field (days), per rule 40's FixedQuantity control. Keep it as short as the English original: there is little room in the box.
policyRules.fieldUnit.imdb_rating: A short fixed unit word shown in the same box as the number, for a rule on the 'imdb_rating' field (a rating denominator, shown as a fixed suffix after the number box), per rule 40's FixedQuantity control. Keep it as short as the English original: there is little room in the box.
policyRules.fieldUnit.imdb_votes: A short fixed unit word shown in the same box as the number, for a rule on the 'imdb_votes' field (a vote count), per rule 40's FixedQuantity control. Keep it as short as the English original: there is little room in the box.
policyRules.fieldUnit.recent_watchers: A short fixed unit word shown in the same box as the number, for a rule on the 'recent_watchers' field (a person count), per rule 40's FixedQuantity control. Keep it as short as the English original: there is little room in the box.
policyRules.fieldUnit.release_age: A short fixed unit word shown in the same box as the number, for a rule on the 'release_age' field (days), per rule 40's FixedQuantity control. Keep it as short as the English original: there is little room in the box.
policyRules.fieldUnit.size_bytes: A short fixed unit word shown in the same box as the number, for a rule on the 'size_bytes' field (gigabytes), per rule 40's FixedQuantity control. Keep it as short as the English original: there is little room in the box.
policyRules.fieldUnit.watchers_all_time: A short fixed unit word shown in the same box as the number, for a rule on the 'watchers_all_time' field (a person count), per rule 40's FixedQuantity control. Keep it as short as the English original: there is little room in the box.
policyRules.keepEditor.blurb: The help paragraph above the keep-rule editor. "outright" and "lean toward keeping" are each wrapped in their own tag (`<outright>`, `<lean>`) for emphasis; keep both phrases consistent with how the rest of the editor names these two rule strengths.
policyRules.keepEditor.hiddenUnverified: A notice listing lists that exist but have not synced yet, so they cannot be picked as a keep rule. `{n}` decides singular/plural; `{count}` is the same count spelled out in the plural branch. "Settings → Lists" uses an arrow, which is fine to keep as-is (rule 21).
policyRules.keepEditor.hiddenWrongType: A notice listing lists hidden because they hold the wrong media type for this policy (a movie list on the TV policy, or the reverse). `{n}`/`{count}` are the same count in each plural branch, and the nested `{mediaType}` selects which media type those lists actually hold.
policyRules.keepEditor.leanSentence: A keep rule's summary when it leans toward keeping rather than keeping outright. `{field}` is the field's translated name, `{direction}` selects between "the less, the safer" and "the more, the safer" depending on which direction of the value is protective, and `{value}` is where the rule reaches its full effect.
policyRules.keepEditor.lowersScore: A trailing clause on a lean keep rule, stating how many points it removes. `{n}` is the point amount; `{isRamp}` selects between "up to N" (a sliding scale) and "by N" (a flat amount).
policyRules.keepEditor.noListsWrongType: Shown when the operator has no list of the media type this policy needs. `{mediaType}` appears twice, selecting "movies"/"shows" the first time and "movie"/"show" the second (a plural noun, then a singular one naming the list type to add). "Settings → Lists" is a path with an arrow, fine to keep.
policyRules.keepEditor.onListSentence: A keep rule's summary when it matches one exact list by name. `{list}` is the operator-typed list name, never translated.
policyRules.keepEditor.removeConditionAr: A screen-reader-only label on the button that deletes an outright keep rule. `{rule}` is that rule's own already-composed summary sentence.
policyRules.keepEditor.removeLeanAriaLab: A screen-reader-only label on the button that deletes a lean keep rule. `{sentence}` is the rule's own composed summary, `{isRamp}` selects "up to " or nothing, and `{n}` is the point amount being removed.
policyRules.rampValueGb: A plain data-size value used on a ramp control's endpoint label. `{gb}` is a number already formatted to one decimal place; "GB" is the unit and stays in Latin script even where the rest of the sentence is translated, matching how sizes are shown elsewhere in the app.
policyRules.removeEditor.removeAriaLabel: A screen-reader-only label on the button that deletes a removal (condemn) rule. `{rule}` is that rule's own already-composed summary sentence.
policyRules.removeEditor.weightFlat: A removal rule's flat point badge, "+N points". `{n}` is the point amount.
policyRules.removeEditor.weightRamp: A removal rule's sliding-scale point badge, "up to +N points". `{n}` is the maximum point amount.
policyRules.suggestInput.valueAriaLabel: A screen-reader-only label on a rule's value input, when the field offers autocomplete suggestions. `{field}` is that field's translated name.
