policySim.comparisonLine: In the policy simulator, compares the current draft policy against the last real scan. `{beforeCount}` and `{afterCount}` are each a plain item count, individually wrapped in bold tags (`<beforeNum>`, `<afterNum>`).
policySim.histogram.bucketTooltip: A tooltip on one bar of the simulator's score histogram. `{low}` and `{high}` are the score range that bucket covers (an en dash between them is fine, it is not the em dash rule 21 forbids), and `{n}` is how many items fall in it.
policySim.moreLeftAlone: A trailing line under the simulator's list of newly-flagged titles, when there are more than fit on screen. `{n}` is how many additional titles the last scan already left alone and this draft also leaves alone, so they are not repeated in the list above.
policySim.pace.noCaps: The simulator's pace line when per-run limits are turned off. `{days}` is how many days a newly flagged title would show as "leaving soon" before it is actually removable.
policySim.pace.withCaps: The simulator's pace line when per-run limits are on. `{items}` and `{bytes}` are the formatted per-run caps (a count and a data size), `{days}` is the same leaving-soon duration as `policySim.pace.noCaps`.
policySim.progressStatus: The simulator's progress line while a simulation is running. `{detail}` is an already-composed status phrase (what step it's on) and `{percent}` is a plain whole-number percentage.
policySim.scanStartFailed: An error notice when starting a policy simulation failed outright. `{error}` is the server's own plain-language error text, not composed from a catalog id, so it may already be in English regardless of the app's language.
policySim.staleReason.gathers_differentl: The policy simulator's notice when the candidate policy being edited differs from the one the last scan actually ran under (a changed weight or gate), so the shown counts are stale. {media_type} selects between 'movies' and 'TV' wording.
policySim.staleReason.in_progress_not_re: The policy simulator's notice when the last scan did not record mid-binge progress data, so simulated counts involving that protection cannot be shown. No params.
policySim.staleReason.seasons_not_record: The policy simulator's notice when the last scan did not record the season-level data the current season rules need, so simulated counts cannot be shown. No params.
reapConfirm.arm.off: Shown on the Reap confirmation screen when deletion is turned off, so nothing here can run yet. Tells the operator to enable it under Policy → Deletion. <strong> and <em> are formatting only; keep the arrow.
reapConfirm.arm.typePhrase: Label above the confirmation box on the Reap screen. {phrase} is the exact phrase the operator must retype before Reaper deletes anything, shown inside a <code> tag. Translate the sentence, never the phrase itself.
reapConfirm.arm.unknown: Shown on the Reap confirmation screen when Reaper could not tell whether deletion is armed. Tells the operator to check Policy → Deletion and reload the page.
reapConfirm.bar.announceEnded: Screen-reader announcement when a reap run ends. `phase` picks one of three outcomes: error, aborted, or a normal finish. {souls} is the already-formatted item count (see format.souls, Reaper's own word for the titles it removes); {bytes} is an already-formatted size like "4.2 GB".
reapConfirm.bar.endedLabel: Short status label on the reap progress bar once a run ends. `phase` picks one of three outcomes: error, aborted, or a normal finish.
reapConfirm.bar.errorSuffix: A fragment appended after another sentence on the reap progress bar, never shown alone. {error} is the raw error text from the failed step, in whatever language it arrived in. Keep the leading period and space.
reapConfirm.bar.freedSuffix: A fragment appended after a count on the reap progress bar, never shown alone. {bytes} is an already-formatted size. Keep the leading comma and space.
reapConfirm.bar.reapingCount: Progress bar label while a reap run is in progress. {done} and {total} are plain item counts.
reapConfirm.bar.removedFreed: Progress bar summary once items have been removed. {souls} is the already-formatted item count (format.souls); {bytes} is an already-formatted size.
reapConfirm.bar.stopError: Shown if the operator clicks Stop on a running reap and the stop itself fails. {error} is the raw error text from the failed request.
reapConfirm.failed.body: Shown when a reap run stops on an error. {error} is the raw error text. Tells the operator that anything already removed is gone, and to check the review queue after the next scan.
reapConfirm.freedAmount: A short fragment reporting freed disk space. {bytes} is an already-formatted size.
reapConfirm.heldBack: Reports items Reaper could not measure and so will not delete. {souls} is the already-formatted item count; {n} is the same count as a plain number, used only to pick the plural and pronoun forms (is/are, its/their, it/them).
reapConfirm.practiceRun.failed: Shown when a practice run (a dry run of the reap, nothing deleted) itself fails to complete. {message} is the raw failure text.
reapConfirm.progress.announceTick: Screen-reader progress announcement during a reap run. {pct} is a whole-number percentage.
reapConfirm.progress.count: Progress bar's item counter. {done} and {total} are plain counts. "souls" is Reaper's own word for the items being reaped, used the same way on every reap surface (format.souls); keep it consistent with reapConfirm.reapCount and reapConfirm.progress.valueText.
reapConfirm.progress.valueText: Accessible value text read out for the reap progress bar. {pct} is a whole-number percentage; {done} and {total} are plain counts.
reapConfirm.reapCount: Label on the main confirm button that starts a reap. {souls} is the already-formatted "N souls" count of items about to be removed (format.souls).
reapConfirm.result.reclaimed: Result line after a reap finishes. {souls} is the already-formatted item count; the sentence reads as "<count> reclaimed".
reapConfirm.result.sparedAtLastMoment: A fragment appended to the reap result line, never shown alone. {n} is a plain count of items spared in the last seconds before deletion (someone started watching). Keep the leading comma and space.
reapConfirm.result.unmeasuredSuffix: A fragment appended to the reap result line, never shown alone. {n} is a plain count of items whose size was unknown. Keep the leading comma and space.
reapConfirm.sparedAmount: A fragment reporting how many items were spared, never shown alone. {n} is a plain count. Keep the leading comma and space.
reapConfirm.summary: Main summary line on the Reap confirmation screen, before the run starts. {souls} is the already-formatted item count; {bytes} is the already-formatted size. Explains that the run removes the smallest items first, tests itself on the first item before continuing, deletes through Sonarr and Radarr, and adds an import exclusion so a deleted title does not silently come back.
reapPlan.breakdown.allowanceUnknown: Shown on the Reap plan page when Reaper cannot say how many unmeasured (unknown-size) titles it is allowed to remove. {count} is a plain count of titles on the list that cannot be measured; {n} is the same count, used only to pick the plural of "title".
reapPlan.breakdown.expiredSpares: Line on the Reap plan page reporting titles kept by a spare that has run out. {count} is a plain count; {n} is the same count, used only to pick the plural forms (title is/are, a spare that expired/spares that expired, it/them). Tells the operator this reap will not remove them, and the next scan judges them again. <strong> is formatting only.
reapPlan.breakdown.handReapedHeld: Line on the Reap plan page reporting hand-marked reaps that are on hold and will not run yet. {count} is a plain count; {n} is the same count, used only to pick the plural forms (reap you marked is/are, it/them).
reapPlan.breakdown.plexNotice: A tip on the Reap plan page pointing the operator at the "Leaving Soon" Plex notice feature, under Settings → Plex. “Leaving Soon” is a feature name and stays as written; <btn> wraps the path as a link.
reapPlan.breakdown.reapCountMeta: A fragment on the Reap plan page giving the count of titles about to be removed, wrapped in <strong>. {count} is a plain count; {n} is the same count, used only to pick the plural of "title". Ends with a comma, because it leads into another sentence.
reapPlan.breakdown.reasonsOf: A fragment on the Reap plan page reading "of N titles", used after another count. {count} is a plain count; {n} is the same count, used only to pick the plural of "title".
reapPlan.breakdown.split: Line on the Reap plan page splitting the total into movies and TV seasons. {moviesCount} and {seasonsCount} are plain counts; {movies} and {seasons} are the same two counts, used only to pick their plural forms. Explains the run order: smallest items first, the test item first of all.
reapPlan.breakdown.unmeasuredAllowed: Line on the Reap plan page reporting titles that cannot be measured but are still allowed to be removed, up to the operator's own unknown-size limit. {count} is a plain count; {n} is the same count, used only to pick the plural of "title".
reapPlan.breakdown.unmeasuredHeld: Line on the Reap plan page reporting titles that cannot be measured and so will not be removed at all. {count} is a plain count; {n} is the same count, used only to pick the plural forms (title/titles, it/them).
reapPlan.degraded.notice: Shown on the Reap plan page when the underlying scan came back incomplete, so no plan can be built from it. {reason} is another composed sentence naming what went wrong. <strong> is formatting only. Tells the operator to fix the source and scan again.
reapPlan.page.blurb: Introductory line on the Reap plan page. <em> is formatting only. Explains that a plan only records what a reap would do, that a practice run is available, and that nothing is removed yet.
reapPlan.report.moreOutcomes: Shown at the end of a long practice-run report when there are more results than fit on screen. {count} is a plain count of the remaining ones.
reapPlan.report.walkedAll: Result line after a practice run (a dry run; nothing was actually removed) where every planned item ran with no items skipped. {soulsCount} is the plain count wrapped in a <walkedNum> tag for styling; "walked" is Reaper's word for stepping an item through every safety check without sending anything.
reapPlan.report.walkedSkipped: Result line after a practice run where some planned items would have been skipped. {soulsCount} and {skippedCount} are plain counts, each wrapped in its own styling tag (<walkedNum>, <skipNum>). Same "walked" wording as reapPlan.report.walkedAll.
reapPlan.steps.more: Shown at the end of a long list of plan steps when there are more than fit on screen. {count} is a plain count; {n} is the same count, used only to pick the plural of "step". Reassures the operator that the run still covers every step, only the display is truncated.
reapPlan.summary.heldBackUnknownSize: Summary line on the Reap plan page reporting items held back because their size is unknown. {soulsCount} is the already-formatted item count; {n} is the same count, used only to pick the plural and pronoun forms (is/are, its/their, it/them). Same meaning as reapConfirm.heldBack, on the plan page instead of the confirm screen.
reapPlan.summary.planLine: Main summary line on the Reap plan page. {souls} is the already-formatted item count; {bytes} is the already-formatted size. Same wording as reapConfirm.summary's opening clause: smallest items first, the first item is a test that stops the run if it does not go as planned.
reapPlan.summary.staleRun: Warning on the Reap plan page when the plan was built from an older scan than the latest one, so it may list titles the operator has since protected. <btn> wraps a button that builds a fresh plan.
reapPlan.summary.staleUnknown: Warning on the Reap plan page when Reaper cannot tell whether the plan matches the latest scan. <btn> wraps a button that builds a fresh plan.
reviewQueue.aboutCardAria: Screen-reader label on a review queue card's info control. {title} is the title of the movie or show on that card.
reviewQueue.announce.showingCollection: Screen-reader announcement when the review queue switches to showing one Plex collection. {collection} is the collection's own name, exactly as it is set in Plex.
reviewQueue.bulkCountCardsItems: Label on the review queue's bulk-selection toolbar, reporting how many cards and how many underlying items are selected (a show card can hold several season items). {cards} and {items} are plain counts, each wrapped in its own styling tag (<cardsNum>, <itemsNum>); {c} and {i} are the same two counts, used only to pick their plural forms.
reviewQueue.bulkCountSelected: Label on the review queue's bulk-selection toolbar when a plain count of selected items is enough (no card/item split). {n} is a plain count wrapped in a <num> tag for styling.
reviewQueue.bulkFailuresMessage: Shown after a bulk action on the review queue when some items could not be updated. {n} is a plain count driving the plural (1 item / # items). Tells the operator the failed items are still selected so the action can be retried.
reviewQueue.collCounts: Line on a Plex collection card in the review queue. {plexCount} is the number of titles Plex reports in the collection; {scannedCount} is how many of them the last scan actually saw.
reviewQueue.collFateInLane: A fragment on a collection card reading "in <lane>", naming which review lane (Kept or Limbo) the collection's members fall in. {lane} is one of the queue's own lane names and is composed from the catalog, not typed English; keep the sentence able to take any lane name.
reviewQueue.collectionsNamed: Heading over review queue results filtered to Plex collections whose name matches a search. {search} is the operator's own typed search text, shown in quotes.
reviewQueue.condemnedOfTotal: Summary line on a show or collection card. {condemned} and {total} are plain counts; {size} is an already-formatted size, describing what would be removed out of the total.
reviewQueue.dormantPillTitle: Tooltip on the amber "not watched" pill shown on a condemned card. {span} is an already-formatted humanized duration, like "3 weeks" or "5 years, 9 months".
reviewQueue.filterChipTitle: Tooltip on an active filter chip in the review queue's toolbar. {label} is the filter's own display text, such as a genre or library name.
reviewQueue.hiddenLine.abstain: Notice on the review queue's Limbo tab when items are filtered out of view but still exist in that lane. {n} drives the plural (1 item in Limbo is hidden. / # items in Limbo are hidden.). "Limbo" is Reaper's own name for this lane and stays untranslated as a term, but the surrounding sentence translates normally.
reviewQueue.hiddenLine.condemn: Notice on the review queue's condemned tab when items are filtered out of view but still exist in that lane. {n} drives the plural (1 condemned item is hidden. / # condemned items are hidden.).
reviewQueue.hiddenLine.protect: Notice on the review queue's Sanctuary (kept) tab when items are filtered out of view but still exist in that lane. {n} drives the plural (1 protected item is hidden. / # protected items are hidden.).
reviewQueue.libraryChipTitle: Tooltip on a Plex library filter chip in the review queue. {library} is the Plex library's own name, such as one the operator typed when setting up their server.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.dayRowLabel: One row's label in the spare-length dropdown menu (Spare for N days). {n} is a plain day count.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.ownReapedHe: Note on a season row the operator marked to reap, explaining it is held for now even though its whole show is spared. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.ownReapedRe: Note on a season row the operator marked to reap, explaining it will still be removed even though its whole show is spared. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.ownSparedSt: Note on a season row the operator spared by hand, explaining it stays kept even though the whole show is set to reap, and what clearing the spare does. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.showAlsoRea: Note on a season row explaining that clearing this season's own override will not save it, because the whole show is also set to reap. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.showAlsoSpa: Note on a season row explaining that clearing this season's own override will not remove it, because the whole show is also spared. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.showReapHel: Note on a season row explaining the whole show is set to reap but this particular season is being held for now, with a link to undo the show-level decision. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.showReapWil: Note on a season row explaining the whole show is set to reap and this season will be removed with it, with a link to undo the show-level decision. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.showSparedK: Note on a season row explaining the whole show is spared, so this season is kept too, with a link to undo the show-level decision. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.spareAgainT: Tooltip on a spare control once its spare has expired. {expiredOn} is another composed sentence saying when it expired. Invites the operator to spare it again.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.spareForDay: Tooltip on the spare button. {n} is the currently selected day count. Mentions the small arrow control that changes the length.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.spareJudgeA: Tooltip on an active spare control. {until} is another composed sentence saying when the spare runs out and Reaper judges the item again.
reviewQueue.overrideControls.sparedCount: Label on a spared item's control showing how long is left. {short} is an already-formatted short duration, like "3d".
reviewQueue.overrideControls.sparedLeftA: Screen-reader label with the same meaning as reviewQueue.overrideControls.sparedCount. {short} is an already-formatted short duration, like "3d".
reviewQueue.queueTotal: The review queue's own totals line, built from several optional fragments. {itemsCount} is a plain item count wrapped in <itemsNum>; {n} is the same count, used only for its plural; {sizeText} is an already-formatted size wrapped in <sizeNum>; `freed` and `hasUnknown` are yes/no switches that turn optional clauses ("would be freed", an unknown-size count wrapped in <unknownNum>) on or off; {unknownCount} and {u} are a further count and its plural switch for that last clause.
reviewQueue.removeFilterAria: Screen-reader label on a filter chip's remove (×) control. {label} is that filter's own display text.
reviewQueue.requestedBy: Line on a card showing who requested the title through the operator's requests app. {who} is that person's own display name from the requests app.
reviewQueue.scoreTitle: Tooltip on a card's score badge. {score} is the item's removal score, an integer out of 100 (the scale Reaper's whole scoring system uses).
reviewQueue.searchChipLabel: Label on the active search filter chip, the operator's own typed search text shown in quotes.
reviewQueue.seasonCount: A season count fragment, such as in a show's summary. {n} drives the plural (1 season / # seasons).
reviewQueue.seasonNumber: Label naming one season row by its number. {n} is the season number as Plex or Sonarr numbers it.
reviewQueue.selectCardAria: Screen-reader label on a card's selection checkbox. {title} is the title of the movie or show on that card.
reviewQueue.selectEverythingMatchingCoun: Button label that selects every item matching the current filters at once, not just the ones currently on screen. {count} is a plain count of how many that will select.
reviewQueue.showInherit.reapAll: Note on a show card set to reap in full, explaining every season below is removed unless individually spared. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.showInherit.reapNone: Note on a show card set to reap where none of its seasons are actually condemned yet, so the reap is recorded but nothing is removed for now. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.showInherit.reapSome: Note on a show card set to reap where only some seasons are removable now; the rest are kept for now unless the operator changes that. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.showInherit.spareExpired: Note on a show card whose whole-show spare has run out, explaining its seasons stay kept until the next scan judges them again. <b> is formatting only.
reviewQueue.showInherit.spared: Note on a show card that is spared as a whole, explaining every season below is kept unless individually reaped. {suffix} is another composed fragment, such as a duration, appended before the closing . is formatting only.
reviewQueue.showPanel.subtitle: Subtitle under a show's title in the expanded show panel. {n} drives the plural of "season" (1 season / # seasons); {size} is an already-formatted total size.
reviewQueue.showingOfTotal: Pagination line reporting how many of the filtered results are currently shown. {shown} and {total} are plain counts.
reviewQueue.spareSelectedForDays: Screen-reader label on the bulk spare action. {n} is the day count the operator selected.
reviewQueue.stopSearchingClearLabel: Screen-reader label on the control that clears an active search. {search} is the operator's own typed search text.
reviewQueue.stripOpenAria: Screen-reader label on a season strip's open control. {name} is the show's title; {lane} is the season's review lane name (composed from the catalog, e.g. Sanctuary or Limbo).
reviewQueue.stripTitle: Tooltip on a season strip square. {name} is the show's title; {lane} is the season's review lane name; {overrideNote} is an optional composed fragment naming a hand override in force on that season, or empty when there is none.
reviewQueue.whyScoredAria: Screen-reader label on the control that opens the why-panel for a card. {title} is the item's title; {score} is its removal score out of 100.
safetyBanner.armed: The safety banner shown everywhere in the app while deletion is turned on, meaning Reaper is allowed to remove approved media through Sonarr and Radarr. This is a safety-critical, always-visible notice; `<strong>` wraps the leading claim and should stay wrapped around the equivalent emphasized phrase in translation. Sonarr and Radarr are product names and stay untranslated.
safetyBanner.readOnly: The safety banner shown everywhere in the app while deletion is turned off: Reaper can review media but cannot remove anything yet. `<strong>` wraps the leading claim. `<btn>` wraps a link/button phrase that takes the operator to the setting that turns deletion on; keep it around an equivalent short phrase. "Policy → Deletion" is a path through the app's own menus and should stay as an arrow-separated path, not be turned into a sentence.
safetyBanner.readOnlyNoLink: The same read-only safety banner as `safetyBanner.readOnly`, for a context with no button to render (a screen where that link would not work). `<strong>` wraps the leading claim the same way. "Policy → Deletion" is again a path through the app's menus, kept as an arrow-separated path.
safetyBanner.recovery: The safety banner shown while the server is in recovery mode, which holds off all deletion regardless of the armed setting. `<strong>` wraps the leading claim.
safetyBanner.unknown: The safety banner shown when Reaper cannot reach the server to confirm whether deletion is armed, so it tells the operator to treat it as armed (the cautious assumption) until it can check. `<strong>` wraps the leading claim. `<btn>` wraps a link/button phrase to the setting where the operator can check for themselves; "Policy → Deletion" is a menu path and stays as an arrow-separated path.
safetyBanner.unknownNoLink: The same unknown-safety-state banner as `safetyBanner.unknown`, for a context with no button to render. `<strong>` wraps the leading claim. "Policy → Deletion" is again a menu path, kept as an arrow-separated path.
scales.balanceBar.ariaNoReclaim: Screen-reader label for a person's usage bar on the Scales screen, when nothing of theirs would be reclaimed by a scan. {used} is a formatted byte size (for example "4.2 GiB"), shown as-is.
scales.balanceBar.ariaReclaim: Screen-reader label for a person's usage bar on the Scales screen, when some of their titles would be reclaimed. {used} and {reclaim} are both formatted byte sizes, shown as-is.
scales.board.acrossPeople: A fragment on the Scales screen stating how many people a total is spread across. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
scales.board.card.earningKeep: A note on a person's Scales card: their kept titles are still being watched enough to justify the space. <usedSize> wraps a formatted byte size; keep the tag, translate only the words around it.
scales.board.card.openBreakdown: Screen-reader label for the button that opens one person's detail panel on the Scales screen. {name} is that person's own display name (their Plex or requests-app username), shown as-is.
scales.board.card.reclaimChip: A small chip on a person's Scales card showing how much space a scan would free from their titles. {amount} is a formatted byte size, shown as-is.
scales.board.card.summary: A one-line summary on a person's Scales card: how many titles they requested and how much space was granted to them. <reqCount> and <grantedSize> each wrap one number; keep both tags, translate only the words around them.
scales.board.card.toReclaim: A note on a person's Scales card naming how much space and how many titles a scan would reclaim from them. <reclaimSize> wraps a formatted byte size; keep the tag. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {n} argument).
scales.board.reclaimableSub: A subtitle on the Scales screen's summary card, giving the total title count a scan would reclaim across everyone. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
scales.collectionChip.inCollection: A chip on a title in the Scales screen naming the Plex collection it belongs to. {name} is that collection's own name as set in Plex, shown as-is.
scales.collectionChip.showOthers: A "show more" link under a title's collection chips, when it belongs to more than one and only the first is shown. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {rest} argument).
scales.meta.alsoAskedBy: A fragment noting other people who also requested the same title, on a person's detail panel in the Scales screen. {list} is a comma-joined list of their display names, built in code rather than as an ICU list; keep the comma-and-space style, since it is not re-joined per language.
scales.meta.andOthers: A fragment summarizing a name list that was cut short, of the shape "name, name, and N others". {shown} is the already-formatted lead names, shown as-is. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {n} argument).
scales.meta.arrived: A fragment on a title row in the Scales screen stating when it arrived in the library. {date} is a formatted date, shown as-is.
scales.meta.asked: A fragment on a title row in the Scales screen stating when it was requested. {date} is a formatted date, shown as-is.
scales.meta.askedBy: A fragment naming who requested a title, on a person's detail panel in the Scales screen. {list} is a comma-joined list of display names, built in code rather than as an ICU list; keep the comma-and-space style.
scales.notInScan.leadSame: The heading of the "not in the last scan" panel, for a person whose request count and title count are the same number. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {n} argument).
scales.notInScan.leadSplit: The heading of the "not in the last scan" panel, for a person whose requests span more titles than the request count alone (for example a season request covering several episodes). {requests} is a plain request count, already formatted. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. (applies to the {n} argument).
scales.notInScan.leadWithDetail: The full heading of the "not in the last scan" panel, combining the count sentence with a fixed trailer. {lead} nests `scales.notInScan.leadSame` or `scales.notInScan.leadSplit`.
scales.personPanel.limits.lifetimeReques: A fragment on a person's detail panel stating their all-time request limit. {n} is a plain count of requests, with no time period.
scales.personPanel.limits.text: A fragment on a person's detail panel stating their request limit, optionally per a number of days. {limit} is the limit number, already formatted; {days} is a day count. An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option. nested with An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms. for the day count.
scales.personPanel.notInScanCount: A pluralized request count ("1 request" / "N requests") for titles the last scan did not include, on a person's detail panel. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
scales.personPanel.reclaimableCount: A pluralized title count ("1 title" / "N titles") that a scan would reclaim from this person, on their detail panel. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
scales.personPanel.requestsSummary: A summary line on a person's detail panel: how many requests were in the last scan, and optionally how many more were not. {n} is the count in the scan; {m} is the count left out, shown only when {hasMore} is "yes". An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option.
scales.personPanel.titlesCount: A pluralized title count with an optional "not in the scan" addendum, on a person's detail panel. {n} is the titles counted; {m} is how many of those are not in the last scan, shown only when {hasMore} is "yes". An ICU select: keep the argument name and the option keys (the words before each {...}), translate only the text inside each option. nested with An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms..
scales.personPanel.watched.episodes: A pluralized episode-watch count on a person's detail panel. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
scales.personPanel.watched.movieTimes: A pluralized watch-count fragment for a movie on a person's detail panel ("watched 1 time" / "watched N times"). An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
scales.personPanel.watched.noneSince: A note on a person's detail panel that a title hasn't been watched since a given date. {date} is a formatted date, shown as-is.
scales.unmatchedList.titleCount: A pluralized title count ("1 title" / "N titles") heading the list of requests Reaper could not match to a library item, on the Scales screen. An ICU plural: keep the {n}/{count} argument name, translate only the plural forms.
security.blurb: Introductory text at the top of Settings → Security, explaining what the admin password is for. <strong> is inline emphasis on "Policy → Deletion", the name of another screen in the app; keep that emphasis on the equivalent phrase in translation. "Plex" is a product name and stays untranslated.
security.form.changeFailedError: Shown on the password-change form when saving a new password fails. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
security.form.newPasswordPlaceholder: Placeholder text inside the new-password input box. {min} is the minimum required character count as a whole number.
security.form.setFailedError: Shown when setting the admin password for the first time fails. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
security.form.tooShortError: Live validation message shown while typing a password shorter than the minimum. {min} is the minimum required length; {count} is how many characters have been typed so far. <b> is inline emphasis on the live count; keep the emphasis on the equivalent number in translation.
services.discord.saveError: Shown in the Discord notification settings when saving the webhook URL fails. {error} is the server's own error text, passed through as written. "Discord" is a product name and stays untranslated.
services.discord.testResult.failed: Shown in Settings → Services after the operator tests their Discord webhook and it fails, telling them to check the URL and that the channel still exists. No params.
services.discord.testResult.not_configur: Shown in Settings → Services if a Discord webhook test is attempted with no webhook saved yet. No params.
services.discord.testResult.posted: Shown in Settings → Services after a Discord webhook test succeeds and a test message was posted to the operator's channel. No params.
services.modal.addedAnnouncement: A screen-reader announcement made after adding a connected service (Sonarr, Radarr, Plex, Seerr, or Tautulli). {name} is the name the operator gave that connection.
services.modal.externalUrlHelp: Help text under an optional "external URL" field in the add/edit service form, for services whose links should open at a different address than the one Reaper connects to (e.g. a reverse-proxy hostname). {kind} is the service type's display name, such as "Sonarr" or "Radarr" (a product name, stays untranslated).
services.modal.field.externalUrlPlacehol: Placeholder text inside the external URL field. {kind} is the service type's own short id used only to build an example URL (e.g. "sonarr" in "https://sonarr.example.com"); "example.com" is a placeholder domain and should stay as literal example text, not a real address.
services.modal.folders.noneToMap: Shown in the add/edit service form when there are no Plex libraries of the right kind to map yet. {libKind} selects between "movie" and "TV" depending on the service being configured (Radarr vs. Sonarr); "Plex" is a product name and stays untranslated.
services.modal.folders.pickerAriaLabel: Screen-reader label for the dropdown that maps one of the service's root folders to a Plex library. {path} is a file system folder path, shown as-is from the connected service; it is not user-facing prose, so it should not be translated or reformatted.
services.modal.mapError: Shown in the add/edit dialog for a Sonarr/Radarr/Seerr connection when Reaper reached the service but could not read the lists it needs to offer (root folders, quality profiles). {error} is that service's own plain-language error text, passed through as written: never translate its contents, only the surrounding sentence.
services.modal.missing.host: Live validation message when the hostname/IP field is empty in the add/edit service form. {willDo} is a nested fragment, either "add it" or "save it" (services.modal.willDo.add / services.modal.willDo.save), completing the sentence.
services.modal.missing.key: Live validation message when the API key field is empty in the add/edit service form. {willDo} is the same nested add/save fragment as services.modal.missing.host.
services.modal.missing.name: Live validation message when the connection's name field is empty in the add/edit service form. {willDo} is the same nested add/save fragment as services.modal.missing.host.
services.modal.requesters.pickerAriaLabe: Screen-reader label for a dropdown that links a requests-app (Seerr) connection to a Sonarr/Radarr instance. {name} is the connection's own name; {is4k} selects whether " 4K" is appended, for a 4K-specific profile; {serviceKind} is the service type's display name (e.g. "Sonarr").
services.modal.savedAnnouncement: A screen-reader announcement made after saving changes to a connected service. {name} is the connection's own name.
services.modal.titleAdd: The add/edit service modal's heading when adding a new connection. {kind} is the service type's display name, such as "Sonarr" or "Plex" (a product name, stays untranslated).
services.panel.addKindButton: Button on the Services screen that opens the add-connection form for one service type. {label} is that service type's display name, e.g. "Sonarr".
services.panel.card.cancelRemoveAria: Screen-reader label for the button that backs out of removing a connected service, on its confirm-remove step. {name} is the connection's own name.
services.panel.card.confirmRemoveAria: Screen-reader label for the button that confirms removing a connected service. {name} is the connection's own name.
services.panel.card.removeAria: Screen-reader label for a connected service's remove (delete) button, before confirmation. {name} is the connection's own name.
services.panel.card.removeFailed: Shown on the Services screen when removing a connection fails. {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
services.panel.card.removedAnnouncement: A screen-reader announcement made after a connected service is removed. {name} is the connection's own name.
services.panel.card.testAriaIdle: Screen-reader label for a connected service's "Test" button when idle (not currently testing). {name} is the connection's own name.
services.panel.card.testAriaPending: Screen-reader label for a connected service's "Test" button while a connection test is running. {name} is the connection's own name. The ellipsis (…) is intentional, matching a busy/in-progress state.
services.panel.card.testFailed: Shown on the Services screen when a connection test cannot even run (as opposed to running and reporting a failed result). {message} is the server's own error text, passed through as written.
services.test.badgeVersion: A small fragment appended after a connection test's result badge, showing the connected service's version. {version} is a version string reported by that service (e.g. Sonarr's own version number). Keep the leading space and parentheses.
services.test.sentence: Composes a connection test's result line: a fixed lead word ({lead}, e.g. "Connected" or "Failed") followed by the service's own detail text ({detail}), with an optional version suffix ({version}, services.test.badgeVersion's sibling wording). The colon joins lead and detail; adapt the joiner if your language does not use a colon this way.
services.test.version: A fragment showing a connected service's version, spelled out (as opposed to services.test.badgeVersion's compact form). {version} is a version string reported by that service. Keep the leading space and parentheses.
setup.connect.removeFailedError: An inline error on the first-run setup wizard's connection step, shown when removing a connection (Sonarr, Radarr, Plex, and so on) failed. `{message}` is the error text from the server, already in plain language.
setup.connect.removingAria: An accessible status announcement read by screen readers while a connection is being removed on the setup wizard's connection step. `{name}` is the operator's own name for that connection.
setup.connect.restoreDoorLead: The lead sentence of a callout on the setup wizard's connection step, offering to restore a backup from an existing Reaper install instead of setting up from scratch. `<strong>` wraps the leading question.
setup.password.adminNote: Help text on the setup wizard's password step, telling the operator their local account will initially be named "admin" and can be renamed later. `admin` is the literal, fixed account name shown as it will actually appear, so it should not be translated.
setup.password.minHelp: Help text under the password field on the setup wizard's password step, stating the minimum length. `{min}` is the minimum character count, a plain number.
setup.password.saveFailedError: An inline error on the setup wizard's password step, shown when saving the new password failed. `{message}` is the error text from the server, already in plain language.
setup.plex.signedInTo: A confirmation line on the setup wizard's Plex step, shown after signing in, naming the Plex account. `{name}` is the Plex account or server name Plex itself returned.
setup.scan.announceFinishedWithBlocker: An accessible status announcement read by screen readers when the setup wizard's first scan finishes but something still blocks moving on. `{sentence}` is another composed sentence (naming the blocker) inserted after this lead clause; write this lead so it reads naturally followed by another full sentence.
setup.scan.notReadyWarning: A warning on the setup wizard's scan step, shown when the operator has not yet connected the services a scan needs (Tautulli, and one of Radarr or Sonarr). `<btn>` wraps a button phrase that jumps back to the connection step; keep it around an equivalent short phrase. Tautulli, Radarr and Sonarr are product names and stay untranslated.
setup.scan.scanErrorNotice: An inline error on the setup wizard's scan step, shown when the first scan itself failed partway through. `{message}` is the error text from the server, already in plain language.
setup.stepper.progress: The step counter at the top of the setup wizard: "Step 2 of 5". `{n}` is the current step number and `{total}` is the total number of steps, both plain numbers.
shell.docBody.flowchartWithTitle: The caption under a diagram inside the in-app manual, when the diagram has its own title. `{title}` is the diagram's title, taken from the manual's own content and translated separately as part of that content, not here.
shell.docsModal.showingDoc: An accessible status announcement read by screen readers when the in-app manual's viewer switches to showing a different page. `{title}` is that page's title, taken from the manual's own content.
shell.quantityInput.unitLabelWithName: The accessible label for the unit selector half of a number-plus-unit control (see `QuantityInput`, used across policy and settings screens for values like days or gigabytes), when the control has its own accessible name. `{ariaLabel}` is that control's own name, and this key appends the word "unit" to it.
shell.scanBar.degradedNotice: A warning on the Jobs page's scan row, shown when the last scan came back incomplete and Reaper will not act on it. `<strong>` wraps the leading claim. `{reason}` is a plain-language explanation of what went wrong, itself composed from another catalog entry and inserted here as a sentence continuing this one.
shell.scanBar.deltaItems: A fragment comparing this scan's item count with the scan before it: "12 more to remove" or "3 fewer to remove". `{n}` is the difference as a plain formatted number; `{dir}` selects between "more" (an increase) and "fewer" (a decrease). This fragment is joined with others by `shell.scanBar.deltaSummary` and does not stand alone.
shell.scanBar.deltaSize: A fragment comparing this scan's reclaimable size with the scan before it: "1.2 GB more to free" or "400 MB less to free, 2 sizes unknown". `{n}` is a formatted size difference; `{dir}` selects between "more" and "less"; `{qualifier}` is an optional trailing clause (from `shell.scanBar.deltaUnknownQualifier`) noting unmeasured items, or empty. This fragment is joined with others by `shell.scanBar.deltaSummary` and does not stand alone.
shell.scanBar.deltaSummary: The sentence wrapping the scan-to-scan comparison on the Jobs page's scan row: "Compared with the scan before: 12 more to remove, 1.2 GB more to free." `{parts}` is the comma-joined list of fragments from `shell.scanBar.deltaItems` and `shell.scanBar.deltaSize`, already assembled in English punctuation; if your language joins a list differently, note that here rather than editing the join itself.
shell.scanBar.deltaUnknownQualifier: A trailing clause nested inside `shell.scanBar.deltaSize`, noting how many items' sizes could not be measured and so are left out of the size comparison: ", 2 sizes unknown". `{n}` is the count and drives the plural form of "size"/"sizes". Starts with a comma because it is appended directly after another fragment, not shown alone.
shell.scanBar.scanProblem: An inline error on the Jobs page's scan row, shown when the most recent scan (including one run by the schedule, not just one the operator just started) failed. `{error}` is the error text from the server, already in plain language.
shell.scanBar.snapshotSummary: The main summary line on the Jobs page's scan row, stated as one sentence with two emphasized numbers: "1,204 items, 87 would be removed, freeing 12.4 GB." `{itemCount}`, `{condemnedCount}` and `{freedAmount}` are plain formatted numbers/sizes. `<condemned>` and `<freed>` each wrap one of those numbers for emphasis and should stay wrapped around the equivalent number in translation.
shell.scanBar.step.active_streams: A scan's live status line: the sub-step while it reads who is watching right now. No params.
shell.scanBar.step.done: A scan's live status line: the sub-step just before the queue commits, naming how many titles the scan is about to condemn. `{count}` is that number, and the plural follows it.
shell.scanBar.step.history_sync: A scan's live status line: the sub-step while it syncs watch history from Tautulli. No params.
shell.scanBar.step.libraries: A scan's live status line: the sub-step while it reads the movie and TV libraries. No params.
shell.scanBar.step.lists: A scan's live status line: the sub-step while it refreshes protection lists. No params.
shell.scanBar.step.ratings: A scan's live status line: the sub-step while it reads IMDb ratings. No params.
shell.scanBar.step.scoring: A scan's live status line: the sub-step while it scores one title at a time. `{title}` is the title currently being scored, exactly as it is named in Plex.
shell.scanBar.step.seasons: A scan's live status line: the sub-step while it reads TV seasons from Sonarr. No params.
shell.scanBar.step.shelves: A scan's live status line: the sub-step while it updates the Plex Leaving Soon shelves after scoring finishes. No params.
shell.scanBar.step.watch_history: A scan's live status line: the sub-step while it reads watch history. No params.
shell.scanFreshness.degradedNotice: A warning shown on pages that display the last scan's results, when that scan came back incomplete and Reaper will not act on it. `<btn>` wraps a button phrase that jumps to Settings → Jobs to trigger a rescan; keep it around an equivalent short phrase, and keep "Settings → Jobs" as an arrow-separated menu path.
shell.scanFreshness.lastScanned: A status line shown on pages that display the last scan's results, stating when it ran and how large it was: "Last scanned 3 hours ago, 1,204 items." `{date}` is a formatted relative or absolute date/time; `{count}` is a plain formatted number.
shell.scanFreshness.noScanYet: A notice shown on pages that display scan results, when no scan has ever run. `<btn>` wraps a button phrase that jumps to Settings → Jobs to run one; keep it around an equivalent short phrase, and keep "Settings → Jobs" as an arrow-separated menu path.
shell.settings.switchConfirmBackup: A confirmation shown when leaving a settings tab that has an unrestored backup file chosen, warning that switching tabs drops the pending restore. `{pendingLabel}` is the name of the tab the operator is switching to.
shell.settings.switchConfirmGeneric: A confirmation shown when leaving a settings tab that has unsaved changes, warning that switching tabs discards them. `{leavingLabel}` is the name of the tab being left; `{pendingLabel}` is the name of the tab being switched to.
shell.staleRead.line: A notice shown wherever a live status check could not complete in time, so the data on screen may be out of date. `{what}` is a short phrase naming what could not be checked (for example "the Plex connection"), composed from context and inserted into this sentence.
shell.statusChip.exceptSeasons: A qualifying clause on a status chip for a whole TV show, used when some of its seasons carry their own opposing decision: "except 2 seasons". `{n}` is the count of seasons and drives the plural form. This fragment is inserted into other status-chip strings rather than shown alone.
shell.statusChip.reapRequestedKept: A status chip shown on an item the operator marked for removal by hand, but that Reaper is still keeping for now. `{why}` is another composed sentence explaining the reason and is inserted after this lead clause.
shell.statusChip.reapedByHand: A status chip shown on an item the operator marked for removal by hand and that removal will actually happen. `{detail}` is either the "except N seasons" qualifier above or a plain "will be removed" phrase, inserted after this lead clause.
shell.statusChip.sparedByHandWith: A status chip shown on an item the operator chose to keep by hand, with a trailing detail (a countdown, an "except N seasons" qualifier, or a plain "will be kept" phrase). `{suffix}` is that composed detail, inserted after this lead clause.
shell.tagsEditor.removeTag: The accessible label on the remove button for one tag inside a tag-editing control (used for genres, keep-lists, and similar tag fields). `{tag}` is the operator's own tag text, typed by them, not translated.
shell.userMenu.updateAvailableLabel: The accessible label on the account menu button when a Reaper update is available, combining the signed-in username with that fact. `{username}` is the operator's own account name.
signals.addedOfPoints: The Why panel's per-signal row: what a built-in signal actually added to the score, then the ramp it was measured against. `{added}` is the points this row added this scan, already worded ("0", "less than 1", or a number); `{weight}` is the signal's configured maximum; `{scale}` is a nested, already-composed sentence from one of the signals.scale* keys.
signals.nthNewestSeason: An ordinal phrase used in the policy signals card to describe a season's position by recency: "the newest season", "the second-newest season", "the 4th-newest season". `{n}` is the season's rank counting back from the newest and drives the ordinal form (`selectordinal`); keep every branch (`=1`, `=2`, `=3`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `other`) even if your language's ordinal rules group them differently.
signals.ratingValue: A built-in signal's rating bound, worded on the Policy page's ramp labels and the rewatch probe's result (the low-rating signal). `{value}` is the rating to one decimal place, e.g. "6.4"; "IMDb" is the rating source's own name and is not translated.
signals.scaleAboveOrEqual: One of three ways the Policy page states a built-in signal's ramp: the "shortfall" shape, whose sentence runs downward (a rating or watcher-count signal). `{from}` and `{to}` are the signal's own worded bounds, already composed elsewhere in this file (e.g. "IMDb 6.0"); `{weight}` is a plain point count, the signal's configured maximum.
signals.scaleEvenFirst: The Policy page's ramp sentence for a signal whose floor sits below the lowest real value the field can take (the season-rank signal, which starts at 1), so a plain "nothing until" sentence would be false. `{first}` is that lowest value, already worded; `{weight}` and `{to}` are the same shapes as signals.scaleAboveOrEqual.
signals.scaleUntil: The ordinary (non-shortfall) form of the Policy page's ramp sentence, for a signal that charges more the further a value runs past its bound (dormancy, file size). `{from}` and `{to}` are the signal's own worded bounds; `{weight}` is a plain point count.
signals.sizeValueGb: A built-in signal's file-size bound, worded on the Policy page's ramp labels and the rewatch probe's result (the large-file signal). `{value}` is a whole number of gigabytes.
signals.watcherCount: A built-in signal's watcher-count bound, worded on the Policy page's ramp labels and the rewatch probe's result (the few-watchers signal). `{n}` is a plain count driving the ICU plural.
warning.added_before_history: A Policy Editor warning that a keep rule based on all-time watcher counts cannot flag any title added before the operator's watch history began, since Reaper cannot count plays from before that point. {rules} is a plain count of the operator's own keep rules in this situation, driving an ICU plural.
warning.custom_rule_size: A Policy Editor warning that a custom rule removes items for being large, which favors removing popular 4K files over unwanted ones. {rule_name} is the operator's own name for their rule, passed through as typed.
warning.custom_rules_cannot_fire: A Policy Editor warning that one or more custom removal rules based on recent-watcher counts cannot fire, because the watch history does not reach back far enough. {rules} is a plain count driving several ICU plurals in the sentence; {window_days_window} is a humanized window like 'year'; {shortfall} is a nested why.cause.* fragment explaining the shortfall.
warning.dormancy_beyond_history: A Policy Editor warning that the minimum-dormancy protection cannot yet flag anything, because the operator's watch history is shorter than the wait it requires. {days_span} is a humanized duration derived from the configured day count; {shortfall} is a nested why.cause.* fragment explaining the gap.
warning.field_unreadable_for_media: A Policy Editor warning that a rule uses a field Reaper cannot read for the policy's own media type (a movie-only or TV-only field used on the wrong policy), so it never does anything. {kind} selects among protection/rule/keep_rule wording; {named} is 'yes'/'no' selecting whether {rule_name} (the operator's own rule name) is shown in quotes; {field_label} is the field's own label (why.field.*); {media_type} selects between 'seasons' and 'movies'.
warning.graded_keeps_beyond_history: A Policy Editor warning that one or more graded keep rules cannot yet apply their full effect, because the watch history is too short. {scope} selects between a 'window' phrasing and a fallback phrasing for an all-time span; {rules} is a plain count; {names} is a list of the operator's own rule names, each already wrapped by why.rule_name and joined by the composer, never by a hardcoded English word; {total} and {headroom} are plain point counts on Reaper's removal scale; {move} selects which remedy sentence to show (wait, remove, or set a lower value); {window_days_window} and {shortfall} appear only in the window-scoped branch, the same shapes as the warning above.
warning.graded_keeps_exceed_threshold: A Policy Editor warning that the operator's keep rules can together subtract enough points to protect almost everything. {points} and {threshold} are both plain integers on Reaper's 0-100 scale.
warning.horizon_off: A Policy Editor warning shown when the operator has turned off the protection for a title whose unwatched time could not be measured. No params.
warning.in_progress_unreadable: A Policy Editor warning that the mid-binge protection cannot tell who is partway through a show. {hold_days} is the operator's own configured number of days a viewer's place is held, with a special-cased sentence at exactly 0 (held forever, which no history can ever confirm) and a different one for any other value; {hold_days_span} is a humanized duration derived from it; {shortfall} is a nested why.cause.* fragment.
warning.keep_last_all_shows: A Policy Editor warning that the 'keep the last N seasons of requested shows only' setting is actually applying to every show, because no requests app (Seerr) is connected to tell requested and unrequested shows apart. {keep_last} is the operator's own configured season count.
warning.keep_last_too_many: A Policy Editor warning that the configured 'keep the last N seasons' number is so high it protects nearly every show, making TV season pruning ineffective. {keep_last} is the operator's own configured count.
warning.popularity_beyond_history: A Policy Editor warning that the built-in few-watchers protection cannot yet flag anything, because the watch history is shorter than its window. {window_days_window} is a humanized window; {shortfall} is a nested why.cause.* fragment; {remedy} selects between a 'wait' sentence and a 'lower the window' sentence.
warning.popularity_rules_beyond_history: A Policy Editor warning that one or more operator-authored keep rules on recent-watcher counts cannot yet fire, for the same reason as warning.popularity_beyond_history. {rules} is a plain count; {field_label} (singular case only) is the field's own label; {window_days_window} and {shortfall} are the same shapes as the warning above.
warning.popularity_window_short: A Policy Editor warning that the configured recent-watchers window is unusually short, so almost nothing counts as recently watched. {window_days_span} is a humanized duration derived from the operator's own configured day count.
warning.rating_bar_high: A Policy Editor warning that a rating floor is set so high it will protect almost nothing. {floor_tenths} is the operator's own bar to one decimal place; {source_label} is the rating source's display name (why.source.*).
warning.rating_bar_low: A Policy Editor warning that a rating floor is set so low it protects almost everything, likely a mistake (for example typing a 0-10 value where a percentage was meant). {floor_tenths} and {source_label} as above.
warning.rating_bar_percent: A Policy Editor warning specific to a percentage-scale rating source, catching the common mistake of typing an 0-10 number where a percentage was meant. {floor} is the raw stored number; {source_label} is the rating source's display name.
warning.rating_no_sources: A Policy Editor warning that the 'keep well-rated titles' protection is on but has no rating source configured, so it currently protects nothing. No params.
warning.season_conflicts_before_history: A Policy Editor warning that TV season-keep conflicts cannot be detected for shows added before the watch history began, since Reaper cannot compare watcher counts from before that point. No params.
warning.size_points: A Policy Editor warning that the built-in 'large files' signal is adding removal pressure, which favors removing large popular 4K files over unwanted ones. {points} is a plain integer on Reaper's removal scale.
warning.streaming_check_off: A Policy Editor warning that the operator has turned off the check for whether someone is currently watching a title before it reaches the reap list (Reaper still refuses to delete a file mid-play at the last moment either way). No params.
warning.threshold_low: A Policy Editor warning that the configured remove-threshold is low enough to condemn almost everything the protections do not save. {threshold} is the operator's own configured value on Reaper's 0-100 scale.
warning.unmeasured_allowance: A Policy Editor warning that Reaper is allowed to delete a limited number of items it could not measure the size of, so the operator's byte caps will not cover them. {count} is the operator's own configured allowance.
warning.watcher_points_beyond_history: A Policy Editor warning that removal rules based on recent-watcher counts together hold back enough points that nothing can be flagged, because the watch history is too short. {points} and {ceiling} are plain point counts on Reaper's 0-100 scale; {window_days_window} and {shortfall} are the same shapes as the warnings above.
watchReach.reachesBackTo: Shown on the Scales board, a person's detail drawer, and the Why panel wherever the watch mirror's reach is stated: how far back Reaper's watch history goes, so an operator reading a 0% or a "not watched" knows it may only mean the mirror does not reach that far. `{date}` is an already-formatted local date, not a raw timestamp.
