Also composed as {field_label} and {field_subject} inside other why.* sentences, so keep it short and reuse the same wording every time this field is named.
why.field.show_ended: The plain-language label for the policy field 'The show has ended' (a condition an operator can build a rule on in the Policy Editor). Also composed as {field_label} and {field_subject} inside other why.* sentences, so keep it short and reuse the same wording every time this field is named.
why.field.size_bytes: The plain-language label for the policy field 'Size on disk' (a condition an operator can build a rule on in the Policy Editor). Also composed as {field_label} and {field_subject} inside other why.* sentences, so keep it short and reuse the same wording every time this field is named.
why.field.streaming_now: The plain-language label for the policy field 'Being watched right now' (a condition an operator can build a rule on in the Policy Editor). Also composed as {field_label} and {field_subject} inside other why.* sentences, so keep it short and reuse the same wording every time this field is named.
why.field.watchers_all_time: The plain-language label for the policy field 'People who have ever watched it' (a condition an operator can build a rule on in the Policy Editor). Also composed as {field_label} and {field_subject} inside other why.* sentences, so keep it short and reuse the same wording every time this field is named.
why.field.whitelisted: The plain-language label for the policy field 'On a list you curate yourself' (a condition an operator can build a rule on in the Policy Editor). Also composed as {field_label} and {field_subject} inside other why.* sentences, so keep it short and reuse the same wording every time this field is named.
why.field_unreadable: The why-panel's row for a field Reaper could not read for this item. {field_check} is a nested why.check.* fragment naming the field. A lowercase fragment: 'could not read {field_check}'.
why.field_value: The why-panel's row showing a field's own current numeric value. {field_label} is the field's own label (why.field.*); {value, number} is the raw number, locale-formatted. Shaped as a label-colon-value pair: keep the colon.
why.hand_spare: A lowercase fragment meaning the operator manually spared this item by hand. No params, no trailing punctuation: it is inserted into a larger sentence built elsewhere.
why.keep_no_lists: A lowercase fragment for a list-membership condition matching 'none of your lists'. No params, nested inside a larger why-panel sentence such as why.custom_fired's {cond}.
why.keep_not_on_list: A lowercase fragment for a list-membership condition matching a specific list the item is NOT on. {name} is the operator's own list name, shown in quotes exactly as they typed it.
why.keep_on_list: A lowercase fragment for a list-membership condition matching a specific list the item IS on. {name} is the operator's own list name, shown in quotes exactly as they typed it.
why.keep_unchecked: The why-panel's row for a keep rule that could not be evaluated at all, kept conservatively rather than dropped. {check} is a nested why.check.* fragment naming what could not be checked. A lowercase fragment: 'kept fully: could not check {check}'.
why.keep_unchecked_cause: The same row as why.keep_unchecked, with a reason attached. {check} is a nested why.check.* fragment; {cause} is a nested why.cause.* fragment. Keep the colon between them.
why.kept_safe.ambiguous: The why-panel's lead sentence when an item is kept because it looks like more than one thing in Plex, so Reaper cannot be sure it is judging the right file. No params.
why.kept_safe.conflicted: The why-panel's lead sentence when an item is kept because Plex and Sonarr/Radarr describe it differently. {media} selects between the movie wording (Plex vs. Radarr, a file) and the TV wording (Plex vs. Sonarr, a show); only one branch renders.
why.kept_safe.coverage: The why-panel's lead sentence when an item is kept because too little of its evidence could be read to score it with confidence. No params.
why.kept_safe.match_unreadable: The why-panel's lead sentence when an item is kept because Reaper found a Plex match for it but could not read what that match actually was. No params.
why.kept_safe.unmatched: The why-panel's lead sentence when an item is kept because it could not be found in Plex at all. No params.
why.misconfigured: A short lowercase fragment flagging a stored custom rule that no longer validates (for example a field that was removed). No params, no trailing punctuation.
why.none_recorded: The why-panel's row for a field with no value on record at all. {field_label} is the field's own label (why.field.*). Shaped as a label-colon-value pair, where the value half is the fixed words 'none recorded': keep the colon.
why.panel.backToShow.defaultTitle: The fallback subject used by why.panel.backToShow.label when the show's own title is not available. A short noun phrase, not a full sentence.
why.panel.backToShow.label: A link label in the why-panel, back from a season's own panel to its show. {title} is either the show's own title or the fallback why.panel.backToShow.defaultTitle.
why.panel.explanationUnreadable: Shown in the why-panel when the stored explanation for this item could not be read, so no reasons can be shown until the next scan. No params.
why.panel.fallback.failure: Shown in the why-panel when fetching the reasons for an item fails outright. Tells the operator to close the panel and try again. No params.
why.panel.fallback.loading: Shown briefly in the why-panel while its data is first being fetched. No params.
why.panel.fallback.waiting: Shown in the why-panel during a longer wait for its data, a heavier fallback than why.panel.fallback.loading for the same state. No params.
why.panel.gates.checkedBlurb: A short caption under the why-panel's 'Protections it cleared' list, noting the numbers shown are the ones the scan actually used. No params.
why.panel.gates.checkedTitle: The heading over the why-panel's list of protections that were checked and did not hold this item back. No params.
why.panel.gates.firedBlurb: A short caption under the why-panel's 'What spared it' list, noting that any one of these protections is enough on its own. No params.
why.panel.gates.firedTitle: The heading over the why-panel's list of protections that actually kept this item. No params.
why.panel.gates.showCount: A 'show more' toggle label in the why-panel's protection lists. {count} is a plain pluralized count of hidden rows; the singular case reads 'Show 1', the plural 'Show all N'.
why.panel.head.openInPlex: A link label in the why-panel's header, opening this title in Plex. Product name: keep 'Plex' untranslated.
why.panel.head.radarr: A link label in the why-panel's header, opening this title in Radarr. Product name: leave 'Radarr' untranslated.
why.panel.head.seerr: A link label in the why-panel's header, opening this title's request in Seerr. Product name: leave 'Seerr' untranslated.
why.panel.head.sonarr: A link label in the why-panel's header, opening this title in Sonarr. Product name: leave 'Sonarr' untranslated.
why.panel.head.tautulli: A link label in the why-panel's header, opening this title in Tautulli. Product name: leave 'Tautulli' untranslated.
why.panel.heldBackSizeUnknown: Shown in the why-panel when an item is held back from removal because Sonarr/Radarr reported no size for it. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.keeps.blurb: A short caption over the why-panel's 'Leaning toward keeping' section, when keep rules lowered the score with no specific before/after numbers to show. No params.
why.panel.keeps.blurbWithScores: Same caption as why.panel.keeps.blurb, with the actual numbers. {from} and {to} are plain integers on Reaper's 0-100 scale, the score before and after the keep rules applied.
why.panel.keeps.heading: The heading over the why-panel's section listing keep rules that lowered this item's score. No params.
why.panel.keeps.uncheckedNote: A note in the why-panel explaining that a keep rule Reaper could not evaluate was still treated as if it kept the item, the safe default. <em> is emphasis only; keep it around the same word.
why.panel.keptNotice.ambiguous: The why-panel's notice when an item is kept because it looks like more than one thing in Plex. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.keptNotice.conflicted: The why-panel's notice when an item is kept because Plex and Sonarr/Radarr describe it differently. {mediaType} selects between the movie wording (a file, Radarr) and the TV wording (a show, Sonarr); the select appears twice in the sentence and must branch the same way both times.
why.panel.keptNotice.heading: A short heading in the why-panel over a notice explaining an item was kept out of caution rather than by a specific protection. No params.
why.panel.keptNotice.unmatched: The why-panel's notice when an item is kept because it could not be found in Plex, so Reaper cannot tell whether anyone still watches it. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.leftForYou.blurb: A caption over the why-panel's 'Left for you to decide' section, explaining these items were too close a call or could not be checked. A standalone paragraph, no params.
why.panel.leftForYou.couldntCheck: A line in the why-panel's 'Left for you to decide' section. {checks} is a nested, comma-joined list of why.check.* fragments naming what could not be checked.
why.panel.leftForYou.heading: The heading over the why-panel's section for protections left for the operator to decide by hand. No params.
why.panel.matchCandidates.lead: The why-panel's lead-in line before a list of possible Plex matches for an ambiguous title. {n} is a plain pluralized count of candidates found.
why.panel.matchCandidates.plexLabel: A per-row label in the why-panel's match-candidates list, naming Plex as the source of that candidate. {numbered} is 'yes'/'no' selecting whether {n} (the candidate's own number) is appended, for when there is more than one; the word 'Plex' is a product name and stays untranslated.
why.panel.matchCandidates.tautulliLabel: Same shape as why.panel.matchCandidates.plexLabel, naming Tautulli instead. Product name: leave 'Tautulli' untranslated.
why.panel.mediaLabel.season: A short label the why-panel uses for a TV season row, as opposed to a movie. No params.
why.panel.mergedListing.chip: A small chip in the why-panel showing how many times this title is listed in Plex. {n} is a plain integer. Keep the multiplication sign compact; this is a chip, not a sentence.
why.panel.mergedListing.title: The tooltip/title text behind why.panel.mergedListing.chip, spelled out as a full sentence. {n} appears twice and must be the same number both times: how many Plex listings, and that a watch on any one of them counts toward all of them.
why.panel.meta.runtime: A short fragment showing a title's runtime in minutes, in the why-panel's metadata row. {minutes} is a plain integer. Keep the abbreviation short; this sits beside other small metadata chips.
why.panel.onListSince: Shown in the why-panel for an item on a leaving-soon or similar tracked list, with the date it was added and what keeps it there. {when} is a formatted date. A standalone sentence.
why.panel.ratings.imdbLabel: A short label on the why-panel's IMDb rating badge. Product name: leave 'IMDb' untranslated.
why.panel.ratings.imdbTitleNoVotes: The tooltip text on the why-panel's IMDb rating badge when no vote count is available. Product name: leave 'IMDb' untranslated.
why.panel.ratings.imdbTitleWithVotes: The tooltip text on the why-panel's IMDb rating badge when a vote count is available. {score} is the rating, already formatted; {votes} is a plain vote count. Product name: leave 'IMDb' untranslated.
why.panel.ratings.rtAudienceLabel: A short label on the why-panel's Rotten Tomatoes audience-score badge. 'Rotten Tomatoes' is a product name and stays untranslated; 'audience' may be translated.
why.panel.ratings.rtAudienceTitle: The tooltip text on the same badge as why.panel.ratings.rtAudienceLabel, noting it opens a Rotten Tomatoes search when clicked. Same product-name rule.
why.panel.ratings.rtCriticsLabel: A short label on the why-panel's Rotten Tomatoes critics-score badge. 'Rotten Tomatoes' is a product name and stays untranslated; 'critics' may be translated.
why.panel.ratings.rtCriticsTitle: The tooltip text on the same badge as why.panel.ratings.rtCriticsLabel, noting it opens a Rotten Tomatoes search when clicked. Same product-name rule.
why.panel.ratings.tmdbLabel: A short label on the why-panel's TMDb rating badge. Product name: leave 'TMDb' untranslated.
why.panel.ratings.tmdbTitle: The tooltip text on the why-panel's TMDb rating badge. Product name: leave 'TMDb' untranslated.
why.panel.ratings.traktLabel: A short label on the why-panel's Trakt rating badge. Product name: leave 'Trakt' untranslated.
why.panel.ratings.traktTitle: The tooltip text on the why-panel's Trakt rating badge, noting it opens the title on Trakt. Product name: leave 'Trakt' untranslated.
why.panel.rewatch.heading: The heading over the why-panel's rewatch-probability section. No params.
why.panel.rewatch.measured: The why-panel's sentence stating the measured rewatch rate for titles like this one. {n} and {k} are plain counts (comparable titles measured, and how many were watched again); {mediaType} selects between 'shows' and 'titles'; {pct} is a plain integer percentage.
why.panel.rewatch.noHistory: The why-panel's fallback when there is not enough overall watch history to compute a rewatch rate. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.rewatch.thin: The why-panel's fallback when too few comparable titles exist to compute a reliable rewatch rate. {mediaType} selects between 'shows' and 'titles'.
why.panel.ruleTag: A small tag label in the why-panel marking a row as coming from one of the operator's own custom rules, as opposed to a built-in one. No params.
why.panel.shell.errorHeading: A generic error heading shown if the why-panel itself fails to render. No params.
why.panel.signals.addedLegend: A legend label in the why-panel's signals chart, for the portion of the score added by signals. No params.
why.panel.signals.arguedTitle: The heading over the why-panel's list of signals arguing to remove this item. No params.
why.panel.signals.blurb: A short caption under why.panel.signals.arguedTitle, explaining these are reasons to believe nobody will watch it again. No params.
why.panel.signals.coverageBlurb: A caption in the why-panel stating what share of the scoring evidence could actually be read. {pct} is a plain integer percentage.
why.panel.signals.coverageBlurbWithFloor: Same as why.panel.signals.coverageBlurb, adding the operator's own required minimum. {pct} as above; {floorPct} is the operator's own configured coverage floor as a plain integer percentage.
why.panel.signals.didntApply: A 'show more' toggle in the why-panel's signals list, for signals that did not apply to this item. {count} is a plain integer.
why.panel.signals.heading: The heading over the why-panel's signals section, naming the item's own score. {score} is a plain integer on Reaper's 0-100 scale.
why.panel.signals.heldBackLegend: A legend label in the why-panel's signals chart, for the portion of the score held back by keep rules. No params.
why.panel.signals.moreHidden: A 'show more' toggle in the why-panel's signals list. {count} is a plain integer of hidden rows.
why.panel.signals.moreHiddenWithTotal: Same as why.panel.signals.moreHidden, with the extra score those hidden rows add. {count} is a plain integer of hidden rows; {added} is a plain point count on Reaper's 0-100 scale.
why.panel.signals.pointsAddUp: A short caption in the why-panel's signals section, noting the shown points sum to the score. No params.
why.panel.signals.pointsBeforeKeep: A short caption in the why-panel's signals section, labeling a score shown before keep rules were subtracted. No params.
why.panel.signals.pushedTitle: A short label in the why-panel's signals section for signals pushing to remove the item, a shorter twin of why.panel.signals.arguedTitle used in a tighter layout. No params.
why.panel.signals.uncheckedNote: A note in the why-panel explaining that unchecked signals can only ever lower the score, never raise it. No params.
why.panel.signals.uncheckedTitle: The heading over the why-panel's list of signals that could not be checked. No params.
why.panel.synopsis.less: A 'show less' toggle at the end of a truncated synopsis in the why-panel. No params.
why.panel.synopsis.more: A 'show more' toggle at the end of a truncated synopsis in the why-panel. No params.
why.panel.verdict.condemnedLabel: The why-panel's status label for an item condemned (marked for removal) by the scan. No params.
why.panel.verdict.conflictComparable: The why-panel's verdict note for a season-keep conflict where Reaper made an actual comparison and left the call to the operator. A standalone sentence, no params. The same three-way branch as review.py's chip copy (look.comparable/unknowable/unsettled); keep this and that consistent.
why.panel.verdict.conflictUnknowable: The why-panel's verdict note for a season-keep conflict Reaper could not check at all. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.conflictVague: The why-panel's verdict note for a season-keep conflict that could not be settled, a generic fallback. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.heldAmbiguous: The why-panel's verdict note when the operator asked to remove an item by hand but it looks like more than one thing in Plex, so the hand reap is held. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.heldConflicted: Same situation as why.panel.verdict.heldAmbiguous, for when Plex and Sonarr/Radarr describe the item differently instead. {mediaType} selects between the movie wording (a file, Radarr) and the TV wording (a show, Sonarr), appearing twice and branching the same way both times.
why.panel.verdict.heldLabel: The why-panel's status label for an item currently kept, pending further evidence. No params.
why.panel.verdict.heldStreamingNow: The why-panel's verdict note when the operator asked to remove an item by hand, but it is being watched right now, so the hand reap is held for now. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.heldUnknown: The why-panel's verdict note when the operator asked to remove an item by hand, but Reaper cannot yet confirm it is safe, so the hand reap is held. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.heldUnmanaged: The why-panel's verdict note when the operator asked to remove an item by hand, but no app manages the file, so there is no safe way to do it. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.heldUnmatched: The why-panel's verdict note when the operator asked to remove an item by hand, but Reaper could not find it in Plex, so it cannot tell which file to remove. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.limboLabel: The why-panel's status label for an item in Limbo, Reaper's product name for the not-yet-condemned holding state. Product name: leave 'Limbo' untranslated.
why.panel.verdict.limboNote: The why-panel's explanatory note for an item in Limbo: not condemned because it scored below the operator's threshold or too little could be checked, and the file stays kept. 'Limbo' is a product name and stays untranslated; the rest of the sentence translates normally.
why.panel.verdict.needsLookLabel: The why-panel's status label for an item flagged 'Needs a look', the season-conflict hold. No params.
why.panel.verdict.reapedByHandLabel: The why-panel's status label for an item the operator marked for removal by hand, with nothing holding it back. No params.
why.panel.verdict.reapedByHandNote: The why-panel's explanatory note for the same reapedByHand state. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.sanctuaryLabel: The why-panel's status label for an item in Sanctuary, Reaper's product name for the protected state. Product name: leave 'Sanctuary' untranslated.
why.panel.verdict.sanctuaryOverridable: The why-panel's explanatory note for a Sanctuary item the operator could still manually reap. <strong> wraps emphasis; keep it around the same clause. Explains the score does not matter here, only a hand reap could remove it.
why.panel.verdict.sanctuaryStructural: Same as why.panel.verdict.sanctuaryOverridable, for a Sanctuary item that even a hand reap cannot remove (a structural protection). Same <strong> handling.
why.panel.verdict.spareActive: The why-panel's note for an item the operator manually spared, currently active. {phrase} is a nested countdown fragment from format.spareLeft/format.spareUntil (for example '3 days left' or 'Kept until Jan 5'), already a complete clause.
why.panel.verdict.spareForever: The why-panel's note for an item the operator spared with no expiration. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.spareSeasonExpired: The why-panel's note for a TV season whose own spare has run out. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.spareSeasonPhrase: Same shape as why.panel.verdict.spareActive, for a season-level spare. {phrase} is the same kind of nested countdown fragment.
why.panel.verdict.spareShowForever: The why-panel's note for a season kept because the whole show is spared with no expiration. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.verdict.spareShowPhrase: Same shape as why.panel.verdict.spareActive, for a season kept by a show-level spare that does expire. {phrase} is the same kind of nested countdown fragment.
why.panel.verdict.sparedByHandLabel: The why-panel's status label for an item the operator manually spared. No params.
why.panel.verdict.thresholdClause: A short clause appended to another sentence in the why-panel, naming the operator's own threshold. {threshold} is a plain integer on Reaper's 0-100 scale. Starts with a comma: it is meant to continue a sentence, not start one.
why.panel.watchBlind.done: Shown in the why-panel after the operator accepts using only currently visible plays for a title whose earlier watch data became unreadable. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.watchBlind.notice: The why-panel's explanation of 'watch-blind': plays Reaper recorded earlier for this title are no longer readable, most often because the file was re-added to the library. A standalone paragraph, no params.
why.panel.watchBlind.saveError: Shown in the why-panel if accepting the watch-blind notice fails to save. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.panel.watchBlind.useButton: The button label accepting the watch-blind notice (why.panel.watchBlind.notice) and judging the title on what is visible now. No params.
why.panel.watchBlind.useHelp: Help text bound directly under why.panel.watchBlind.useButton, clarifying the choice applies to this title only. No params.
why.panel.watchBlind.using: A brief in-progress label shown on why.panel.watchBlind.useButton while the choice is being saved. No params.
why.popularity_few: The why-panel's row for the built-in few-watchers signal, when a small number of people watched it recently. {count} is a plain pluralized count; {window_days_window} is a humanized window like 'year'; {floor} is the operator's own configured minimum count needed to keep it on this evidence alone.
why.popularity_nobody: The why-panel's row for the built-in few-watchers signal, when nobody watched it recently. {window_days_window} is a humanized window like 'year'. A standalone sentence.
why.popularity_watched: A lowercase fragment version of the popularity evidence, nested inside a larger why-panel sentence. {count} is a plain pluralized count; {window_days_window} is a humanized window.
why.rating_bar: A short fragment naming the operator's own rating bar for one source, shaped '{floor_fixed1} on {source_label}'. {floor_fixed1} is a rating to one decimal place; {source_label} is the source's display name (why.source.*). Nested inside a larger rating sentence.
why.rating_bar_pct: Same as why.rating_bar, for a percentage-scale rating source: shaped '{source_label} {pct}%'. {pct} is a plain integer percentage.
why.rating_bar_votes: Same as why.rating_bar, for a source with a minimum vote requirement: adds '{votes, number}+ votes' after the bar. {votes} is the operator's own configured minimum vote count.
why.rating_cleared: The why-panel's row for the well-rated protection when it fired. {clauses} is one or more nested rating clauses (why.rating_value.*/why.rating_bar.* family), joined by the composer, never by a hardcoded English word. A lowercase fragment: 'well rated: {clauses}'.
why.rating_cleared_some: The why-panel's row for the well-rated protection when it partially fired: some of the operator's rating bars were cleared but not all of them. {cleared} and {missed} are each nested, comma-joined lists of rating clauses. Keep the comma separating the two clauses.
why.rating_miss_below: A nested rating clause for a rating that came in below the operator's own bar. {value} is a nested why.rating_value.* fragment; {floor_fixed1} is the operator's own bar to one decimal place.
why.rating_miss_below_pct: Same as why.rating_miss_below, for a percentage-scale source. {value} as above; {floor_pct} is the operator's own bar as a plain integer percentage.
why.rating_miss_none: A nested rating clause for a source with no rating recorded at all for this title. {source_label} is the source's display name; {bar} is a nested why.rating_bar.* fragment naming the operator's own configured bar.
why.rating_miss_votes: A nested rating clause for a rating that had too few votes to count. {value} is a nested why.rating_value.* fragment; {need, number} is the operator's own configured minimum vote count.
why.rating_missed: The why-panel's row for the well-rated protection when it did not fire at all. {clauses} is a nested, comma-joined list of rating-miss clauses (the why.rating_miss_*. family). A standalone sentence: keep the trailing period.
why.rating_none_set: The why-panel's row for the well-rated protection when no rating bar is configured to keep anything. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.rating_value: A nested rating clause showing a title's own rating on one source. {value_fixed1} is the rating to one decimal place; {source_label} is the source's display name (why.source.*).
why.rating_value_pct: Same as why.rating_value, for a percentage-scale source: shaped '{source_label} {pct}%'. {pct} is a plain integer percentage.
why.rating_value_votes: Same as why.rating_value, with the vote count shown too. {value_fixed1} and {source_label} as above; {votes} is a plain pluralized vote count.
why.returned_came_back: The why-panel's row for the came-back protection, when the title left the library and was re-added and is currently held. {days_left_span} is a humanized duration derived from a raw day count, the time left on the hold.
why.returned_came_back_ours: Same as why.returned_came_back, for the case where Reaper itself was the one that removed it before. {days_left_span} as above.
why.returned_no_record: The why-panel's row for the came-back protection when Reaper has no record of this title ever leaving and returning. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.returned_not_returned: The why-panel's row for the came-back protection when the title has never left the library and come back. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.returned_past_hold: The why-panel's row for the came-back protection when its hold period has expired. {days_span} and {hold_days_window} are both humanized durations, derived from raw day counts: how long ago it came back, and the operator's own configured hold length.
why.rewatch_count: The why-panel's row showing how many times a title has been watched again. {media} selects between 'Watched again N times' (TV) and 'Watched N times' (movies); {n} is a plain pluralized count.
why.rewatch_count_many: The why-panel's fallback row for a very high rewatch count, shown instead of a specific number. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.rewatch_keep_few: A nested rewatch-evidence clause: a small, exact rewatch count with nothing more to say about it. {count} is a plain integer.
why.rewatch_keep_fired: A nested rewatch-evidence clause for the rewatch-probability keep signal firing: the title has been rewatched and Reaper judges it likely to be watched again. {count} is a plain integer.
why.rewatch_keep_fired_recent: Same as why.rewatch_keep_fired, with a recency added. {count} is a plain integer; {last_days_span} is a humanized duration derived from a raw day count, since the most recent rewatch.
why.rewatch_keep_never: A nested rewatch-evidence clause for a title with no recorded rewatches. {media} selects between 'Never watched again here' (TV) and 'Never watched here' (movies).
why.rewatch_keep_stale: A nested rewatch-evidence clause: the title was rewatched, but not within the operator's own recent window. {count} is a plain integer; {window_days_window} is a humanized window like 'year'.
why.rewatch_no_history: The why-panel's row for the rewatch-probability signal when there is not enough overall watch history to compute one. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.rewatch_thin: The why-panel's row for the rewatch-probability signal when too few comparable titles exist to compute a reliable rate. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.rewatch_under_floor: The why-panel's row for the rewatch-probability signal when the measured rewatch rate for similar titles came in under the operator's own keep threshold. {n} and {k} are plain counts (comparable titles measured, and how many were rewatched, driving an ICU plural on {k}); {floor_pct} is the operator's own threshold as a plain integer percentage.
why.rewatch_watched_again: A lowercase fragment version of the rewatch-probability evidence, nested inside a larger why-panel sentence. {k} and {n} are the same plain counts as why.rewatch_under_floor.
why.rule_name: Wraps an operator's own rule name in quotes wherever it is quoted inside another why.* sentence, shaped '"{name}"'. {name} is the operator's own typed text, passed through as written: never translate it, only keep the quoting convention your language uses.
why.season_keep.airing: The why-panel's protection-fired row for a season kept because the newest season of a show that is still running. The same underlying reason the status chip shows more tersely as chip.text.kept.season.airing and chip.sentence.kept.season.airing; keep the wording of this one and those consistent.
why.season_keep.first: The why-panel's protection-fired row for a season kept because the earliest season on disk, so there is somewhere to start. The same underlying reason the status chip shows more tersely as chip.text.kept.season.first and chip.sentence.kept.season.first; keep the wording of this one and those consistent.
why.season_keep.incomplete: The why-panel's protection-fired row for a season kept because episodes are missing from this season. The same underlying reason the status chip shows more tersely as chip.text.kept.season.incomplete and chip.sentence.kept.season.incomplete; keep the wording of this one and those consistent.
why.season_keep.keep_all: The why-panel's protection-fired row for a show kept entirely because it has too few seasons to prune: it has {total} seasons on disk (a plain count), which is at or under the operator's own keep-last-{keep_last} setting (also a plain count), so every season is kept. The same reason the status chip shows as chip.text.kept.season.keep_all.
why.season_keep.keep_last: The why-panel's protection-fired row for a season kept by the keep-last-N seasons rule: {keep_last} is the operator's configured number of newest seasons to keep, {rank} is this season's own rank counting back from the newest (1 = newest). Both plain integers. The same reason the status chip shows as chip.text.kept.season.keep_last.
why.season_keep.midbinge: The why-panel's protection-fired row for a season kept because a viewer is part-way through the show. The same underlying reason the status chip shows more tersely as chip.text.kept.season.midbinge and chip.sentence.kept.season.midbinge; keep the wording of this one and those consistent.
why.season_keep.specials: The why-panel's protection-fired row for a season kept because specials are never auto-pruned. The same underlying reason the status chip shows more tersely as chip.text.kept.season.specials and chip.sentence.kept.season.specials; keep the wording of this one and those consistent.
why.season_prunable: The why-panel's row for a TV season Reaper found eligible for removal under the keep-last/keep-first season rules, with nothing else protecting it. A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.signal_imdb: The why-panel's row for the built-in IMDb-rating signal, showing the title's own rating. {value_tenths} is the rating to one decimal place. A lowercase fragment.
why.signal_imdb_none: The why-panel's row for the built-in IMDb-rating signal when no rating is recorded. A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.signal_imdb_unreadable: The why-panel's row for the built-in IMDb-rating signal when the rating data could not be read. A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.signal_season_rank: The why-panel's row for the built-in season-rank signal, naming a season's position from the newest as an ordinal ('the newest season', 'the second-newest season', and so on). {rank} is the raw rank (1 = newest); use your language's own ordinal forms rather than translating the English ones literally.
why.signal_season_special: The why-panel's row for the built-in season-rank signal when the season is a special (not one of the show's numbered seasons). A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.signal_season_unreadable: The why-panel's row for the built-in season-rank signal when Reaper could not tell which season number this is. A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.signal_size: The why-panel's row for the built-in file-size signal, showing the file's own size. {gb} is the size in gigabytes, already formatted. A lowercase fragment.
why.signal_size_none: The why-panel's row for the built-in file-size signal when no size is recorded. A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.signal_size_unreadable: The why-panel's row for the built-in file-size signal when the size could not be read. A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.signal_unwatched: The why-panel's row for the built-in days-unwatched signal, showing how long it has gone unwatched. {days_span} is a humanized duration derived from a raw day count. A lowercase fragment.
why.signal_unwatched_no_history: The why-panel's row for the built-in days-unwatched signal when there is no watch history to measure it from. A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.signal_watchers_few: The why-panel's row for the built-in few-watchers signal, showing a small recent-viewer count. {count} is a plain pluralized count; {window_days_window} is a humanized window like 'year'. A lowercase fragment.
why.signal_watchers_no_history: The why-panel's row for the built-in few-watchers signal when there is no watch history recorded for this title at all. A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.signal_watchers_none: The why-panel's row for the built-in few-watchers signal when nobody watched it in the operator's own window. {window_days_window} is a humanized window like 'year'. A lowercase fragment.
why.signal_watchers_unchecked: The why-panel's row for the built-in few-watchers signal when it could not be evaluated at all. {window_days_window} is a humanized window; {cause} is a nested why.cause.* fragment naming why. A lowercase fragment.
why.signal_watchers_unreadable: The why-panel's row for the built-in few-watchers signal when the watcher data could not be read, with no more specific cause available. A lowercase fragment, no params.
why.source.imdb: The display name for IMDb, a rating source. Product name: leave 'IMDb' untranslated.
why.source.metacritic: The display name for Metacritic, a rating source. Product name: leave 'Metacritic' untranslated.
why.source.rotten_tomatoes_audience: The display name for Rotten Tomatoes' audience score. 'Rotten Tomatoes' is a product name and stays untranslated; 'audience' may be translated to distinguish it from the critics score below.
why.source.rotten_tomatoes_critic: The display name for Rotten Tomatoes' critics score. 'Rotten Tomatoes' is a product name and stays untranslated; 'critics' may be translated to distinguish it from the audience score above.
why.source.tmdb: The display name for TMDb, a rating source. Product name: leave 'TMDb' untranslated.
why.source.trakt: The display name for Trakt, a rating source. Product name: leave 'Trakt' untranslated.
why.source.tvdb: The display name for TVDB, a rating source. Product name: leave 'TVDB' untranslated.
why.source.unknown: The fallback {source_label} when Reaper cannot tell which rating source a value came from. Not a product name: translate it normally.
why.streaming_nobody: The why-panel's row for the actively-streaming protection when nobody is watching this title right now. A standalone sentence, no params.
why.streaming_now: A lowercase fragment meaning someone is watching this title right now, nested inside a larger why-panel sentence. No params.
